sentences.zh: 熊概，字元節，豐城人。

translations.literal: Xiong Gai, styled Yuanjie, was a man of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Gai, styled Yuanjie, came from Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，隨母適胡氏，冒其姓。

translations.literal: Orphaned in childhood, he followed his mother in marrying into the Hu family and took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he went with his mother when she remarried into the Hu clan and bore their surname.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 十六年擢廣西按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 峒溪蠻大出掠，布政使議請靖江王兵遏之。

translations.literal: The Dongxi tribesmen came out in great force to plunder, and the administration commissioner proposed requesting troops from the Prince of Jingjiang to check them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dongxi tribesmen raided in force, the provincial administration commissioner proposed calling on troops from the Prince of Jingjiang to stop them.

sentences.zh: 概不可，曰：「吾等居方面，寇至無捍禦，顧煩王耶？

translations.literal: Gai would not agree, saying: "We hold regional posts—when bandits come and we cannot defend, must we trouble the prince?
translations.idiomatic: Gai refused, saying, "We hold frontier posts—if bandits arrive and we cannot defend ourselves, must we trouble the prince?

sentences.zh: 且寇必不至，戒嚴而已。

translations.literal: Moreover the bandits will certainly not come; let us merely go on alert."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the raiders will surely not come; we need only stand on guard."

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: " And afterward it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: And so it turned out.

sentences.zh: 久之，調廣東。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年正月，命以原官與布政使周幹、參政葉春巡視南畿、浙江。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Hongxi, he was ordered to retain his original office and, with Administration Commissioner Zhou Gan and Vice Commissioner Ye Chun, to tour and inspect the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Hongxi, he was ordered to keep his present rank and, together with Administration Commissioner Zhou Gan and Vice Commissioner Ye Chun, tour the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 初，夏原吉治水江南還，代以左通政趙居任，兼督農務。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xia Yuanji returned from managing waterways in Jiangnan, Zuo Tongzheng Zhao Juren replaced him, concurrently supervising agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Xia Yuanji returned from river works in Jiangnan, Left Assistant Minister Zhao Juren succeeded him and also oversaw agricultural affairs.

sentences.zh: 居任不恤民，歲以豐稔聞。

translations.literal: Juren did not care for the people yet each year reported abundant harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Juren neglected the people yet reported bountiful harvests year after year.

sentences.zh: 成祖亦知其誣罔。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu also knew he was deceiving.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu knew as well that he was lying.

sentences.zh: 既卒，左通政嶽福繼之，庸懦不事事。

translations.literal: After Juren died, Zuo Tongzheng Yue Fu succeeded him—timid and weak, attending to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: After Juren died, Left Assistant Minister Yue Fu took his place—a timid, ineffectual man who attended to nothing.

sentences.zh: 仁宗監國時，嘗命概以御史署刑部，知其賢，故有是命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong was overseeing the realm as heir apparent, he had once ordered Gai, while still a censor, to act at the Ministry of Justice and knew his worth—hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Renzong was overseeing the realm as heir apparent, he had once had Gai serve at the Ministry of Justice in his capacity as censor and knew his ability—hence this order.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，幹還，言有司多不得人，土豪肆惡，而福不任職。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month Gan returned and reported that many local offices lacked capable men, local bullies ran rampant, and Fu was not performing his duties.
translations.idiomatic: That August, when Gan returned, he reported that many local offices lacked capable men, local bullies ran wild, and Fu was failing in his post.

sentences.zh: 宣宗召福還，擢概大理寺卿，與春同往巡撫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong recalled Fu and promoted Gai to chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, sending him with Chun as touring pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong recalled Fu and promoted Gai to chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, dispatching him with Chun as touring pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 南畿、浙江設巡撫自此始。

translations.literal: The establishment of touring pacification commissioners for the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The post of touring pacification commissioner for the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang dates from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 浙西豪持郡邑短長為不法。

translations.literal: Powerful men in western Zhejiang held the strengths and weaknesses of prefectures and counties over officials and acted lawlessly.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families in western Zhejiang exploited local officials' weaknesses and acted with impunity.

sentences.zh: 海鹽民平康暴橫甚，御史捕之，遁去。

translations.literal: The salt-worker Ping Kang of Haiyan was extremely violent and overbearing; when a censor arrested him, he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Kang, a salt worker of Haiyan, was notoriously brutal; when a censor arrested him, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 會赦還，益聚黨八百余人。

translations.literal: When an amnesty brought him back, he gathered a band of more than eight hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Released under an amnesty, he rallied a band of more than eight hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 概捕誅之。

translations.literal: Gai captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gai captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 已，悉捕豪惡數十輩，械至京，論如法。

translations.literal: Thereafter he arrested dozens of powerful evildoers, sent them in fetters to the capital, and sentenced them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrested dozens of powerful wrongdoers, sent them in chains to the capital, and had them punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 於是奸宄帖息。

translations.literal: Thereupon treacherous villains subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After that, lawless elements quieted down.

sentences.zh: 諸衛所糧運不繼，軍乏食。

translations.literal: Grain transport to the guard units could not keep up, and the troops lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Grain shipments to the guard units fell behind, and the troops went hungry.

sentences.zh: 概以便宜發諸府贖罪米四萬二千余石贍軍，乃聞於朝。

translations.literal: Gai on his own authority released more than forty-two thousand shi of redemption grain from the various prefectures to feed the troops, then reported it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: On his own authority Gai released more than forty-two thousand shi of redemption grain from the prefectures to feed the troops, then reported the matter to court.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，諭戶部勿以專擅罪概。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and instructed the Ministry of Revenue not to punish Gai for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and told the Ministry of Revenue not to punish Gai for exceeding his authority.

sentences.zh: 概用法嚴，奸民憚之，騰謗書於朝。

translations.literal: Gai applied the law strictly; evil commoners feared him and sent slanderous memorials to court.
translations.idiomatic: Gai enforced the law rigorously, and wrongdoers feared him, so they flooded the court with slanderous reports.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，行在都御史劾概與春所至作威福，縱兵擾民。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, the acting chief censor impeached Gai and Chun for throwing their weight about wherever they went and letting troops harass the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande, the acting chief censor impeached Gai and Chun for abusing their power wherever they went and allowing troops to harass the populace.

sentences.zh: 帝弗問，陰使御史廉之，無所得。

translations.literal: The emperor did not pursue the matter but secretly sent censors to investigate—nothing was found.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no notice and secretly sent censors to investigate, but they found nothing.

sentences.zh: 由是益任概。

translations.literal: From this he trusted Gai all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereafter relied on Gai all the more.

sentences.zh: 明年七月賜璽書獎勵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following year he was granted an imperial letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The following July he received an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 概亦自信，諸當興革者皆列以聞。

translations.literal: Gai also grew confident, and whatever ought to be instituted or abolished he listed and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Gai grew confident as well, reporting every reform he thought necessary.

sentences.zh: 時屢遣部官至江南造紙、市銅鐵。

translations.literal: At the time ministry officials were repeatedly sent to Jiangnan to make paper and purchase copper and iron.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court repeatedly sent ministry officials to Jiangnan to make paper and buy copper and iron.

sentences.zh: 概言水澇民饑，乞罷之。

translations.literal: Gai said floods had left the people hungry and begged that these missions be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gai reported that floods had left the people hungry and asked that the missions be halted.

sentences.zh: 五年還朝，始復姓。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he returned to court and at last resumed his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to court and at last resumed his own surname.

sentences.zh: 亡何，遷右都御史，治南院事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to right chief censor and managed affairs of the southern court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made right chief censor and managed affairs of the southern court.

sentences.zh: 行在都御史顧佐疾，驛召概代領其職，兼署刑部。

translations.literal: The acting chief censor Gu Zuo fell ill; Gai was summoned by courier to take his post and concurrently act at the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When acting chief censor Gu Zuo fell ill, Gai was summoned by courier to take his post and also serve at the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 九年十月錄囚，自朝至日宴，未暇食，忽風眩卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year, while reviewing prisoners from morning until the banquet hour without time to eat, he suddenly suffered vertigo and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year, while reviewing prisoners from morning until the evening banquet without pausing to eat, he was suddenly struck by vertigo and died.

sentences.zh: 賜祭，給舟歸其喪。

translations.literal: Sacrificial offerings were granted and a boat provided to return his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted sacrificial offerings and provided a boat to convey his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 概性剛決，巡視江南，威名甚盛。

translations.literal: Gai's nature was firm and decisive; touring Jiangnan, his renown for authority was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was firm and decisive; on his tour of Jiangnan his authority was widely feared.

sentences.zh: 及掌臺憲，聲稱漸損於初。

translations.literal: When he took charge of the censorate, his reputation gradually fell short of what it had been at first.
translations.idiomatic: Once he headed the censorate, his reputation gradually fell short of its early height.

sentences.zh: 葉春者，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Ye Chun was a man of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Chun was a native of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 起家掾吏，歷禮部郎中兩淮鹽運使，改四川右參政。

translations.literal: He rose from clerk, served as a director in the Ministry of Rites and salt transport commissioner of the Two Huai, and was transferred to right vice commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk, served as a director in the Ministry of Rites and as salt transport commissioner of the Two Huai, and was then made right vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 與概巡撫江、浙諸府。

translations.literal: Together with Gai he served as touring pacification commissioner over the prefectures of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Gai as touring pacification commissioner over the Jiangsu and Zhejiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 既復奉命與錦衣指揮任啟、御史賴英、太監劉寧巡視。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to tour together with Brocade Guard Commander Ren Qi, Censor Lai Ying, and Eunuch Liu Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to tour with Brocade Guard Commander Ren Qi, Censor Lai Ying, and Eunuch Liu Ning.

sentences.zh: 先後凡三蒞浙西，治事於鄉，人無議其私者。

translations.literal: In all he came to western Zhejiang three times; though he conducted affairs in his home region, no one criticized him for private interest.
translations.idiomatic: He came to western Zhejiang three times in all; though he governed in his home country, no one accused him of favoritism.

sentences.zh: 概遷都御史。

translations.literal: Gai was transferred to chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was promoted to chief censor.

sentences.zh: 春同日進刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Chun on the same day was advanced to right vice minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was promoted the same day to right vice minister of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 陳鎰，字有戒，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Yi, styled Youjie, was a man of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi, styled Youjie, came from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the tenth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣副使，歷山東、浙江，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Huguang and served in Shandong and Zhejiang, winning reputation in each.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of Huguang and later served in Shandong and Zhejiang, earning a strong reputation in each post.

sentences.zh: 九年春進右都御史，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he was advanced to right chief censor while continuing to guard the region as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he was promoted to right chief censor while continuing his command as before.

sentences.zh: 秦中饑，乞蠲租十之四，其余米布兼收。

translations.literal: Famine struck within Qin; he begged remission of four-tenths of the land tax, with the remainder collected in grain and cloth together.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Shaanxi, he asked that four-tenths of the land tax be remitted and the remainder collected in grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 時瓦剌也先漸強，遣人授罕東諸衛都督喃哥等為平章，又置甘肅行省名號。

translations.literal: At the time the Oirat leader Esen was growing stronger; he sent men to appoint the commanders of the Han East guards, including Nange, as pingzhang, and also set up the title of Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Oirat leader Esen was growing stronger; he sent envoys to appoint commanders of the Han East guards, including Nange, as pingzhang, and even set up a Gansu Branch Secretariat in name.

sentences.zh: 鎰以聞，請嚴為之備。

translations.literal: Yi reported it and asked that strict preparations be made.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported the matter and urged strict preparations.

sentences.zh: 已，命與靖遠伯王驥巡視甘肅、寧夏、延綏邊務，聽便宜處置。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was ordered, together with Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji, to inspect border affairs in Gansu, Ningxia, and Yansui, with discretion to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered, together with Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji, to inspect border affairs in Gansu, Ningxia, and Yansui, with authority to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 以災沴頻仍，條上撫安軍民二十四事，多議行。

translations.literal: Because disasters recurred frequently, he submitted in detail twenty-four measures to pacify troops and civilians; many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Because disasters struck again and again, he submitted twenty-four detailed measures to reassure troops and civilians, and many were adopted.

sentences.zh: 鎰嘗恐襄、漢間流民嘯聚為亂，請命河南、湖廣、陜西三司官親至其地撫恤之。

translations.literal: Yi once feared that displaced people between Xiang and Han might gather and rise in disorder, and asked that officials of the three provincial administrations of Henan, Huguang, and Shaanxi go in person to the area to comfort and relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi once feared that refugees between the Xiang and Han rivers might gather and rebel, and asked that officials of the Henan, Huguang, and Shaanxi administrations go in person to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 得旨允行，而當事者不以為意。

translations.literal: He received an imperial order approving the plan, but those in charge paid it no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his request, but those in charge paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 王文亦相繼力言有司怠忽，恐遺禍。

translations.literal: Wang Wen also repeatedly urged forcefully that the local offices were negligent and feared leaving disaster behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen also repeatedly warned that local officials were negligent and that disaster might follow.

sentences.zh: 至成化時，乃有項忠之役，人益思鎰言。

translations.literal: By the Chenghua reign there came Xiang Zhong's campaign, and people thought all the more of Yi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Chenghua reign, when Xiang Zhong's campaign took place, did people recall Yi's warnings.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，景帝監國，鎰合大臣廷論王振。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign, Emperor Jingdi oversaw the realm, and Yi joined the grand ministers in court discussion of Wang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern campaign and Emperor Jingdi oversaw the realm, Yi joined the chief ministers in court deliberation on Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 於是振侄王山伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Zhen's nephew Wang Shan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen's nephew Wang Shan was then executed.

sentences.zh: 也先將入犯，以于謙薦，出撫畿內。

translations.literal: When Esen was about to invade, on Yu Qian's recommendation he went out to pacify the metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen was about to invade, on Yu Qian's recommendation he was sent out to pacify the metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 事寧，召還，進左都御史。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was recalled and advanced to left chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored he was recalled and promoted to left chief censor.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，陜西饑，軍民萬余人，「願得陳公活我。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai, Shaanxi suffered famine; more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians said, "We wish to have Lord Chen keep us alive."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai, when Shaanxi suffered famine, more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians cried, "We beg Lord Chen to save our lives."

sentences.zh: 」監司以聞，帝復命之。

translations.literal: " The surveillance and administration commissioners reported it, and the emperor again appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial commissioners reported this, and the emperor sent him back.

sentences.zh: 鎰至是凡三鎮陜，先後十余年，陜人戴之若父母。

translations.literal: By this time Yi had governed Shaanxi three times, more than ten years in all; the people of Shaanxi revered him as they would parents.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yi had governed Shaanxi three times over more than ten years, and the people revered him as they would their parents.

sentences.zh: 每還朝，必遮道擁車泣。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned to court they would block the road, crowd his carriage, and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he returned to court they blocked the road, pressed around his carriage, and wept.

sentences.zh: 再至，則歡迎數百里不絕。

translations.literal: When he came again, the welcome extended for hundreds of li without break.
translations.idiomatic: When he came again, the welcome stretched for hundreds of li without end.

sentences.zh: 其得軍民心，前後撫陜者莫及也。

translations.literal: In winning the hearts of troops and civilians, none who had governed Shaanxi before or after could compare.
translations.idiomatic: In winning the loyalty of troops and civilians, none who governed Shaanxi before or after could match him.

sentences.zh: 三年春召還，加太子太保，與王文並掌都察院。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was recalled, made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and together with Wang Wen jointly headed the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was recalled, made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and shared control of the Censorate with Wang Wen.

sentences.zh: 文威嚴，諸御史畏之若神。

translations.literal: Wen was stern and awe-inspiring; the censors feared him as they would a god.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was stern and formidable; the censors feared him like a deity.

sentences.zh: 鎰性寬恕，少風裁，譽望損於在陜時。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was forgiving; he had little stern authority, and his reputation fell short of what it had been in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was forgiving by nature and exercised little stern authority, and his reputation fell short of what it had been in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年秋以疾致仕。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the following year he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太保，謚僖敏。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous name Ximin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor, with the posthumous name Ximin.

sentences.zh: 天順七年，詔官其子伸為刑部照磨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun an edict appointed his son Shen registrar of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianshun an edict appointed his son Shen registrar of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 李儀，涿人。

translations.literal: Li Yi was a man of Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi came from Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 永樂間以薦舉授戶部主事。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, through recommendation he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign he entered service by recommendation and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗既平高煦，義請去趙王護衛。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuanzong had pacified Gao Xu, Yi asked that the Prince of Zhao's guard units be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xuanzong had put down Gao Xu's rebellion, Yi petitioned to strip the Prince of Zhao of his guard troops.

sentences.zh: 尚書張本亦言：「往歲孟賢謀逆，趙王未必不知。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Ben also said: "In past years Meng Xian plotted rebellion; the Prince of Zhao may not have been unaware.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Ben also argued: "When Meng Xian plotted rebellion in earlier years, the Prince of Zhao can hardly have been ignorant of it.

sentences.zh: 高煦亦謂與趙合謀。

translations.literal: Gao Xu also said that he had conspired with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu himself had said he acted in concert with the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 儀言是。

translations.literal: Yi said this was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Yi agreed.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 既而言者益眾。

translations.literal: Before long those who spoke on the matter grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Before long more and more officials joined in urging the same course.

sentences.zh: 帝封其詞，遣使諭王如儀指。

translations.literal: The emperor sealed their memorials and sent an envoy to instruct the prince as Yi had indicated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sealed up their memorials and sent an envoy to tell the prince to do as Yi had proposed.

sentences.zh: 王即獻護衛，趙卒無事。

translations.literal: The prince immediately surrendered his guard units, and Zhao was ultimately unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: The prince at once gave up his guard troops, and the Prince of Zhao escaped further trouble.

sentences.zh: 儀尋出知九江府，有惠政。

translations.literal: Before long Yi went out to serve as prefect of Jiujiang and governed with benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was soon sent out as prefect of Jiujiang, where his rule brought real benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位之歲，始設諸邊巡撫。

translations.literal: In the year Emperor Yingzong took the throne, frontier touring pacification commissioners were first established.
translations.idiomatic: The year Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne saw the first appointment of touring pacification commissioners on the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史丁璿方督大同、宣府軍儲，而儀以右僉都御史巡撫其地，盛有所建置。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Ding Xuan was then supervising military stores at Datong and Xuanfu, while Yi served as right censor-in-chief touring and pacifying the area, making many constructive arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Ding Xuan was then overseeing military supplies at Datong and Xuanfu, while Yi served as right censor-in-chief touring and pacifying the region and put many useful measures in place.

sentences.zh: 明年請以大同東西二路分責於總兵官羅文、方政。

translations.literal: The next year he asked that the eastern and western routes of Datong be assigned separately to regional commanders Luo Wen and Fang Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he proposed dividing responsibility for Datong's eastern and western routes between the regional commanders Luo Wen and Fang Zheng.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 時朝議遣方政、楊洪出塞，與甘肅將蔣貴、史昭合擊朵兒只伯。

translations.literal: At the time court deliberations proposed sending Fang Zheng and Yang Hong beyond the frontier to join Gansu generals Jiang Gui and Shi Zhao in a combined attack on Toghon Tayisiur.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was debating a plan to send Fang Zheng and Yang Hong beyond the border to join Gansu generals Jiang Gui and Shi Zhao in a joint strike against Toghon Tayisiur.

sentences.zh: 儀言：「四裔為患，自古有之，在備禦有方耳。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Trouble from the four frontiers has existed since antiquity; it lies in having proper defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yi argued: "Disturbances from the border peoples are as old as the realm itself; what matters is sound defense.

sentences.zh: 和寧殘部，窮無所歸，乍臣乍叛，小為邊寇。

translations.literal: The remnant Hening bands, destitute with nowhere to go, now submit and now rebel, making minor border raids.
translations.idiomatic: The surviving Hening bands are exhausted and homeless, submitting one moment and rebelling the next, and pose only a minor border nuisance.

sentences.zh: 邊將謹待之，將自遁，何必窮兵。

translations.literal: If frontier generals treat them carefully, they will flee of themselves—why exhaust the army?
translations.idiomatic: If our border commanders handle them prudently, they will withdraw on their own; why drive the army to exhaustion?

sentences.zh: 萬一乘虛襲我，少有失，適足為笑，乞敕政等無窮追。

translations.literal: Should they seize an opening to strike us and we suffer even a small setback, it would only become a laughingstock; I beg that Fang Zheng and the others be ordered not to pursue to the end.
translations.idiomatic: If they exploit a gap in our defenses and we suffer even a minor defeat, we will only invite ridicule; I ask that Fang Zheng and the others be ordered not to pursue them relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " The advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " His counsel was rejected.

sentences.zh: 督糧參政劉璉不職，儀劾之。

translations.literal: Grain-supply administration commissioner Liu Lian was derelict in duty, and Yi impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lian, the grain-supply administration commissioner, was neglecting his duties, and Yi impeached him.

sentences.zh: 璉乃誣儀淫亂事。

translations.literal: Liu Lian then falsely accused Yi of lewd conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lian then retaliated by accusing Yi of sexual misconduct.

sentences.zh: 適參將石亨欲奏鎮守中官郭敬罪，先咨儀。

translations.literal: Just then assistant regional commander Shi Heng wished to memorialize the crimes of the eunuch Guo Jing, who guarded the region, and first consulted Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time assistant regional commander Shi Heng wanted to memorialize the garrison eunuch Guo Jing for misconduct and sought Yi's advice first.

sentences.zh: 儀誤緘咨牒於核餉主事文卷中，戶部以聞，致亨、敬相奏訐。

translations.literal: Yi mistakenly sealed the consultation memorandum among the documents of the grain-audit director; the Ministry of Revenue reported it, causing Shi Heng and Guo Jing to memorialize against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yi accidentally enclosed the consultation draft in a packet of documents belonging to the grain-audit director; when the Ministry of Revenue reported the matter, Shi Heng and Guo Jing began accusing each other at court.

sentences.zh: 詔儀、璉自陳，而切責敬等。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi and Liu Lian to explain themselves, while sharply rebuking Guo Jing and the others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded Yi and Liu Lian to submit their own accounts while sharply censuring Guo Jing and his associates.

sentences.zh: 璉止停俸二歲。

translations.literal: Liu Lian was only suspended from salary for two years.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lian received no more than a two-year suspension of salary.

sentences.zh: 儀雖引罪，自負其直，詞頗激，遂被劾下吏瘐死。

translations.literal: Though Yi acknowledged guilt, confident in his integrity his words were rather heated; he was then impeached, handed to the judicial officers, and died in prison from illness in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Yi admitted fault, but trusting in his own rectitude he spoke too sharply; he was impeached, turned over to the judicial authorities, and died in custody from illness.

sentences.zh: 正統二年二月也。

translations.literal: This was in the second month of the second year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: It happened in the second month of the second year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 儀居官廉謹，邊人素德之。

translations.literal: Yi was incorrupt and careful in office; the border people had long respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had served with integrity and restraint, and the frontier people had long held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 聞其死，建昭德祠以祀。

translations.literal: On hearing of his death, they built the Zhaode Shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned of his death, they erected the Zhaode Shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 丁璿，上元人。

translations.literal: Ding Xuan was a man of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xuan came from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 永樂中進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination during the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 由御史擢居是職。

translations.literal: From investigating censor he was promoted to this post.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from investigating censor to this office.

sentences.zh: 正統五年將征麓川，命乘傳往備儲餉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, when an expedition against Luchuan was planned, he was ordered to travel by relay horse to prepare stores and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, as preparations began for the Luchuan campaign, he was ordered to travel by courier relay to ready stores and supplies.

sentences.zh: 尋言用兵便宜，遂命撫雲南。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he spoke on the advantages of the military campaign and was then ordered to pacify Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he submitted advice on the conduct of the campaign and was appointed to pacify Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 麓川平，召為左副都御史，所至有聲。

translations.literal: When Luchuan was pacified, he was recalled as left vice chief censor; wherever he went he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: After Luchuan was pacified he was recalled as left vice chief censor, and wherever he served he earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 陳泰，字吉亨，光澤人。

translations.literal: Chen Tai, styled Jiheng, was a man of Guangze.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai, styled Jiheng, came from Guangze.

sentences.zh: 幼從外家曹姓，既貴，乃復故。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his maternal family's surname Cao; once he rose to prominence, he resumed his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he had taken his maternal family's surname, Cao; only after he rose to office did he restore his original surname.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一，除安慶府學訓導。

translations.literal: He placed first in the provincial examination and was appointed instructor at the Anqing Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the provincial examination and was appointed instructor at the Anqing Prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 正統初，廷臣交薦，擢御史，巡按貴州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong, court officials repeatedly recommended him; he was promoted to censor and toured and inspected Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengtong reign court officials repeatedly recommended him; he was promoted to censor and sent to inspect Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 官軍征麓川，歲取土兵二千為鄉導，戰失利，輒殺以冒功，泰奏罷之。

translations.literal: When government troops campaigned against Luchuan, each year two thousand native soldiers were levied as guides; when battles went badly, they were killed to claim credit—Tai memorialized to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Luchuan campaign the army each year drafted two thousand native troops as guides, and when operations failed they were killed to fabricate merit; Tai memorialized to end the practice.

sentences.zh: 再按山西。

translations.literal: He toured Shanxi a second time.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to inspect Shanxi again.

sentences.zh: 時百官俸薄，折鈔又不能即得。

translations.literal: At the time officials' salaries were low, and paper money paid in lieu could not be obtained promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Official salaries were meager at the time, and even the paper notes paid in lieu could not be collected promptly.

sentences.zh: 泰上章乞量增祿廩，俾足養廉，然後治贓汙，則貪風自息。

translations.literal: Tai submitted a memorial asking that salaries be increased to a sufficient amount to sustain integrity; only then, by punishing corruption, would greed naturally cease.
translations.idiomatic: Tai memorialized asking that salaries be raised enough to support honest living; only then, he argued, could corruption be punished effectively and greed brought under control.

sentences.zh: 事格不行。

translations.literal: The proposal was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was rejected and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 六年夏言：「連歲災異，咎在廷臣，請敕御史給事中糾彈大臣，去其尤不職者，而後所司各考核其屬。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he said: "Disasters have recurred year after year; the fault lies with court ministers. I ask that censors and supervising secretaries be ordered to impeach the chief ministers and remove the most derelict, after which each department may examine its subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he argued: "Disasters have struck year after year, and the blame rests with the ministers at court. I ask that censors and supervising secretaries be ordered to impeach the chief ministers and remove the worst offenders, after which each office should review its own subordinates.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 於是御史馬謹等交章劾吏部尚書郭琎等數十人。

translations.literal: Thereupon censors including Ma Jin repeatedly memorialized, impeaching dozens of officials including Minister of Personnel Guo Jin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Censors such as Ma Jin then submitted a stream of memorials impeaching dozens of officials, including Minister of Personnel Guo Jin.

sentences.zh: 已，復出按山東。

translations.literal: Thereafter he went out again to inspect Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out again to inspect Shandong.

sentences.zh: 泰素勵操行，好搏擊。

translations.literal: Tai had always disciplined his conduct and liked to strike hard at wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Tai had always been strict with himself and was eager to prosecute wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 三為巡按，懲奸去貪，威棱甚峻。

translations.literal: Three times serving as touring inspector, he punished the wicked and eliminated corruption; his stern authority was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In three tours as inspector he punished the wicked and uprooted corruption, and his awesome severity was widely feared.

sentences.zh: 九年超擢四川按察使，與鎮守都御史寇深相失。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was abruptly promoted to surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and fell out with garrison chief censor Kou Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was suddenly promoted to surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and came into conflict with garrison chief censor Kou Shen.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，參議陳敏希深指，劾泰擅杖武職，毆輿夫至死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year, administration councilor Chen Min, hoping to please Shen, impeached Tai for having unauthorizedly beaten a military officer and for beating a sedan-chair bearer to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year administration councilor Chen Min, seeking to curry favor with Shen, impeached Tai for unlawfully beating a military officer and for beating a sedan-chair bearer to death.

sentences.zh: 逮刑部獄，坐斬。

translations.literal: He was arrested and held in the Ministry of Justice prison, sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice, and sentenced to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 泰奏辯，大理卿俞士悅亦具狀以聞。

translations.literal: Tai memorialized in his defense; chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review Yu Shiyue also submitted a full report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tai memorialized in his own defense, and Court of Judicial Review chief judge Yu Shiyue also submitted a detailed report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 皆不聽。

translations.literal: None of it was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，赦復官。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor acted as regent, he was pardoned and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor assumed the regency, Tai was pardoned and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 于謙薦守紫荊關。

translations.literal: Yu Qian recommended him to guard Zijing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian recommended him to hold Zijing Pass.

sentences.zh: 也先入犯，關門不守，復論死。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded, the pass was not held, and he was again sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded, the pass was lost, and Tai was again condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 景帝宥之，命充為事官，從總兵官顧興祖築關隘自效。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor pardoned him and ordered him to serve as an official assigned to atone, following regional commander Gu Xingzu in building fortifications to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor spared him and appointed him an official serving at reduced rank to redeem himself, ordering him to follow regional commander Gu Xingzu in building frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年擢大理右少卿，守備白羊口。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he was promoted to right vice minister of justice at the Court of Judicial Review and garrisoned Baiyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai he was promoted to right vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and put in charge of defending Baiyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 四月，都督同知劉安代寧遠伯任禮巡備涿、易、真、保諸城，命泰以右僉都御史參其軍務。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Vice Commissioner-in-chief Liu An replaced Ningyuan Earl Ren Li in patrolling and defending the cities of Zhuo, Yi, Zhen, and Bao; Tai was ordered as right censor-in-chief to participate in the military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Vice Commissioner-in-chief Liu An replaced Ningyuan Earl Ren Li in patrolling and defending Zhuo, Yi, Zhen, Bao, and the other garrison towns; Tai was appointed right censor-in-chief to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年兼巡撫保定六府。

translations.literal: In the third year he also served concurrently as touring pacification commissioner of the six prefectures of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was also made touring pacification commissioner of the six Baoding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 尋命督治河道。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to supervise repair of the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to oversee river works.

sentences.zh: 自儀真至淮安，浚渠百八十里，塞決口九，築壩三，役六萬人，數月而畢。

translations.literal: From Yizhen to Huai'an he dredged channels for one hundred eighty li, closed nine breach points, built three dams, employed sixty thousand laborers, and finished in several months.
translations.idiomatic: From Yizhen to Huai'an he dredged one hundred eighty li of channels, closed nine breaches, built three dams, mobilized sixty thousand laborers, and completed the work in a few months.

sentences.zh: 七年移撫蘇、松。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to pacify Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his pacification duties were moved to Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 天順改元，罷巡撫官，改廣東副使，以憂去。

translations.literal: When Tianshun changed the reign title, touring pacification commissioners were abolished; he was made vice commissioner of Guangdong and left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed to Tianshun the touring pacification posts were abolished; he was made vice commissioner of Guangdong and left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 四川盜起，有言泰嘗蒞其地，有威名，乃復故官，往巡撫。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Sichuan; someone said Tai had once governed there and enjoyed a fearsome reputation, so he was restored to his former rank and sent to pacify the province.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out in Sichuan, officials noted that Tai had once governed there and enjoyed a formidable reputation, so he was restored to his former rank and sent to pacify the province.

sentences.zh: 八年進右副都御史，總督漕運兼巡撫淮、揚諸府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to right vice chief censor, supervising the Grand Canal transport while concurrently pacifying the prefectures of Huai and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to right vice chief censor, put in charge of the Grand Canal transport while also pacifying the Huai and Yang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蒞淮三年，謝政歸。

translations.literal: After three years in the Huai region he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After three years on the Huai frontier he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 成化六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away in the sixth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 李棠，字宗楷，縉雲人。

translations.literal: Li Tang, styled Zongkai, was a man of Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang, styled Zongkai, came from Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the fifth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，為尚書魏源所器。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice and was valued by Minister Wei Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice and won the esteem of Minister Wei Yuan.

sentences.zh: 金濂代源，以剛嚴懾下。

translations.literal: When Jin Lian replaced Yuan, he intimidated subordinates through stern severity.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Lian succeeded Yuan, he kept subordinates in line through harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 棠與辯論是非，譴訶不為動，濂亦器之。

translations.literal: Tang debated right and wrong with him; though rebuked he did not waver, and Lian also came to value him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang argued with him over right and wrong and did not flinch under his scolding; Lian came to respect him as well.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 錄囚南畿，多所平反，進郎中。

translations.literal: Reviewing prisoners in the Southern Metropolitan Region, he reversed many convictions and was promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing prisoners in the Southern Metropolitan Region he overturned many wrongful convictions and was promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 景帝嗣位，超擢本部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was abruptly promoted to vice minister of the same ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, he was suddenly promoted to vice minister of the same ministry.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巡撫廣西，提督軍務。

translations.literal: Before long he toured and pacified Guangxi and supervised military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed to pacify Guangxi and supervise military affairs there.

sentences.zh: 所部多寇，棠以次討平之。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction had many bandits; Tang suppressed them one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was widespread in his jurisdiction, and Tang put down the outbreaks one after another.

sentences.zh: 正己帥下，令行政舉。

translations.literal: He rectified himself and led subordinates; orders were carried out and administration improved.
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined himself and set an example for his subordinates, so that orders were obeyed and governance improved.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，思明土知府黃老，子鈞嗣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, Huang Lao, native prefect of Siming, died and his son Jun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai the native prefect of Siming, Huang Lao, died and was succeeded by his son Jun.

sentences.zh: 庶兄矰使其子殺父子，滅其家，而以他盜為亂告。

translations.literal: His elder half-brother Zeng had his son kill father and son, exterminate the family, and report the disturbance as the work of other bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His elder half-brother Zeng had his own son murder father and son, wipe out the household, and then report the uprising as the work of other bandits.

sentences.zh: 棠檄右參政曾翚副使劉仁宅按其事。

translations.literal: Tang dispatched orders to Right Administration Commissioner Zeng Kun and Vice Commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ordered Right Administration Commissioner Zeng Kun and Vice Commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 翚等誘執矰父子下之獄。

translations.literal: Kun and the others lured and seized Zeng and his son and sent them to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Kun and his colleagues lured Zeng and his son into custody and imprisoned them.

sentences.zh: 矰窘則遣使走京師，上書請帝廢太子立己子。

translations.literal: Hard pressed, Zeng sent an envoy to the capital to memorialize asking the emperor to depose the heir apparent and install his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Zeng sent an envoy to the capital with a memorial asking the emperor to depose the heir apparent and install his own son in his place.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，立擢矰都督同知，出其子於獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, immediately promoted Zeng to vice commissioner-in-chief, and released his son from prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, promptly promoted Zeng to vice commissioner-in-chief, and released his son from prison.

sentences.zh: 事具《懷獻太子》及《土司傳》。

translations.literal: The full account is given in the biographies of the heir apparent Huai/Xian and in the Treatise on Native Officials.
translations.idiomatic: The full story is recorded in the biography of the heir apparent Huai/Xian and in the Treatise on Native Officials.

sentences.zh: 棠既不得竟黃矰獄，郁郁累疏謝病歸。

translations.literal: Tang, unable to bring the case against Huang Zeng to completion, grew depressed and repeatedly memorialized to retire on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to see the case against Huang Zeng through to the end, Tang grew despondent and repeatedly memorialized to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 不攜嶺表一物，以清節顯。

translations.literal: He took not a single thing from beyond the passes and was renowned for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He brought home not a single object from the south and was famed for his spotless integrity.

sentences.zh: 曾翚，字時升，泰和人。

translations.literal: Zeng Kun, styled Shisheng, was a man of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Kun, styled Shisheng, came from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the eighth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 治秦府永興王葬，卻有司饋遺。

translations.literal: Managing the burial of Prince Yongxing of the Qin princely establishment, he refused gifts from the local offices.
translations.idiomatic: While overseeing the burial of Prince Yongxing of the Qin princely establishment, he refused gifts from local officials.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尚書金濂器之，俾典奏牘。

translations.literal: Minister Jin Lian valued him and had him manage memorial drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jin Lian valued him and put him in charge of drafting memorials.

sentences.zh: 有重獄，諸郎不能決，輒以屬翚。

translations.literal: When there were grave cases the various bureau directors could not decide, they regularly assigned them to Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a major case stumped the bureau directors, they would turn it over to Kun.

sentences.zh: 秦王訐巡撫陳鎰狎妓。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin denounced touring pacification commissioner Chen Yi for consorting with courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin accused touring pacification commissioner Chen Yi of consorting with courtesans.

sentences.zh: 翚按得其情，劾藩府誣大臣，鎰得白。

translations.literal: Kun investigated and learned the truth, impeached the princely establishment for slandering a chief minister, and Yi was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Kun investigated and found the truth, impeached the princely establishment for slandering a chief minister, and Chen Yi was exonerated.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he was promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he was promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 以何文淵薦，擢廣西右參政。

translations.literal: On He Wenyuan's recommendation he was elevated to right administration vice commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by He Wenyuan, he was promoted to right administration vice commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 李棠檄翚及副使劉仁宅按黃矰父子。

translations.literal: Li Tang issued orders to Kun and vice commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate Huang Zeng and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang dispatched Kun and vice commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate Huang Zeng and his son.

sentences.zh: 矰使人持千金賄於道，且擁精兵挾之。

translations.literal: Zeng sent men to offer a bribe of a thousand in gold on the road, and also brought picked troops to coerce them.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng sent men to offer a thousand taels of gold in bribes along the way, backed by elite troops meant to intimidate them.

sentences.zh: 二人佯許諾，已，誘執矰下之獄。

translations.literal: The two men feigned agreement; then they lured Zeng into custody and sent him down to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The two men pretended to accept; then they tricked Zeng into custody and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 棠以聞。

translations.literal: Tang reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tang reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，矰以上書擢都督同知，父子俱出獄，翚等太息而已。

translations.literal: Before long, Zeng was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief through a memorial to the throne; father and son were both released from prison, and Kun and the others could only sigh deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zeng was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief after petitioning the throne; father and son were both released from prison, and Kun and his colleagues could only sigh in frustration.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂去。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起官河南御史。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he was recalled and appointed censor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended he was recalled and appointed censor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 清軍者利得軍，多枉及民，翚辨釋甚眾。

translations.literal: Those conducting military household inspections profited from enrolling soldiers and often wrongly implicated civilians; Kun cleared and released very many of them.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors clearing military registers profited from every soldier they enrolled and often wrongfully implicated civilians; Kun exonerated a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 南陽諸府多流戶，眾議驅逐，人情惶急，翚與巡撫撫安之。

translations.literal: The prefectures around Nanyang had many migrant households; public opinion favored expelling them and the people were anxious and alarmed; Kun worked with the touring pacification commissioner to settle and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanyang prefectures had many migrant households; officials debated expelling them and the populace grew fearful, so Kun and the touring pacification commissioner settled and reassured them.

sentences.zh: 天順五年遷山東右布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianshun he was transferred to right administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianshun he was made right administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 民墾田無賦者，奸民指為閑田，獻諸戚畹。

translations.literal: Land that commoners had reclaimed but that carried no tax assessment was pointed out by scoundrels as idle land and presented to imperial in-laws.
translations.idiomatic: Land that peasants had cleared but that owed no tax was denounced by local ruffians as idle land and handed over to imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 部使者來勘，翚曰：「祖制，民墾荒田，永不科稅，奈何奪之？

translations.literal: An envoy from the ministry came to inspect the matter; Kun said, "By ancestral institution, land reclaimed from wasteland by the people is never taxed—how can it be seized?
translations.idiomatic: When a ministry envoy came to investigate, Kun said, "By ancestral law, wasteland reclaimed by the people is never taxed—how can it be seized away?

sentences.zh: 」使者奏如言，乃免。

translations.literal: "The envoy memorialized as Kun had said, and the land was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: "The envoy reported Kun's words to the throne, and the land was spared.

sentences.zh: 成化初，轉左。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was transferred to the left administration commissioner post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chenghua reign he was transferred to left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河南歲饑，計開封積粟多，奏請平糶，貧民賴以濟。

translations.literal: Henan suffered famine that year; calculating that Kaifeng had large stored grain, he memorialized requesting sale at fair price, and the poor relied on this for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan suffered famine that year, noting the large grain reserves in Kaifeng, he memorialized requesting that grain be sold at fair price, and the poor were saved by it.

sentences.zh: 召拜刑部左侍郎，仍食從二品俸。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed left vice minister of the Ministry of Justice, still receiving salary of the secondary second rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and appointed left vice minister of the Ministry of Justice, retaining secondary second-rank emoluments.

sentences.zh: 尋巡視浙江，考察官吏，奏罷不職者百余人，他弊政多所厘革。

translations.literal: Soon he toured and inspected Zhejiang, evaluated officials, memorialized for the dismissal of more than a hundred who were derelict in duty, and reformed many other corrupt practices.
translations.idiomatic: He soon toured Zhejiang to inspect the province, evaluated officials, and memorialized for the removal of more than a hundred incompetent officers; he also reformed many other abuses.

sentences.zh: 還朝，久之，謝病去。

translations.literal: Returning to court, after a long while he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court he eventually resigned, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 翚操行謹，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Kun's conduct was careful, and wherever he went he won a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was scrupulous in conduct and earned a fine reputation wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 及歸，生計蕭然，絕跡公府，鄉人以為賢。

translations.literal: When he returned home his livelihood was bare, he ceased all visits to official residences, and people in his district regarded him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: After he retired home his household lived plainly, he kept away from official circles entirely, and his neighbors regarded him as a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 賈銓，字秉鈞，邯鄣人。

translations.literal: Jia Quan, styled Bingjun, was a man of Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Quan, styled Bingjun, came from Handan.

sentences.zh: 永樂末進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate at the end of the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination near the end of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年授禮科給事中，數有參駁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites, and repeatedly submitted impeachments and rebuttals.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuande he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites, where he repeatedly censured and rebutted official misconduct.

sentences.zh: 英宗踐阼，既肆赦，復命讞在京重囚，多所原宥。

translations.literal: When the Ying Emperor ascended the throne, after a general amnesty had been proclaimed he again ordered review of serious prisoners in the capital, and many were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ying Emperor took the throne, after proclaiming a general amnesty he ordered a review of serious prisoners held in the capital, and many were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 從銓請，推之南京。

translations.literal: At Quan's request this was extended to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: At Quan's request the same review was extended to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，出為大理知府。

translations.literal: When his term expired he went out to serve as prefect of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed prefect of Dali.

sentences.zh: 王驥征麓川，饋運有勞。

translations.literal: When Wang Ji campaigned against Luchuan, Quan had merit in supplying transport.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Ji's campaign against Luchuan, Quan distinguished himself in supplying the army.

sentences.zh: 驥薦之。

translations.literal: Ji recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji recommended him for promotion.

sentences.zh: 麓川平，擢雲南左參政，仍知府事。

translations.literal: When Luchuan was pacified he was promoted to left administration vice commissioner of Yunnan while still handling prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Luchuan was pacified he was promoted to left administration vice commissioner of Yunnan while continuing to administer the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋以驥言，還治司事。

translations.literal: Soon, on Ji's recommendation, he returned to managing the office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, at Ji's recommendation, he returned to managing the provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 正統十二年，左布政使闕，軍民數萬人頌銓，參贊軍務侍郎侯琎等亦疏請，銓遂得擢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengtong the left administration commissioner post was vacant; several tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians praised Quan, and Vice Minister of War Hou Jin and others supervising military affairs also memorialized in request, so Quan was finally promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhengtong, when the left administration commissioner post fell vacant, tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians praised Quan, and military affairs vice minister Hou Jin and others also petitioned on his behalf, and Quan was duly promoted.

sentences.zh: 土官十余部，歲當貢馬輸差發銀及海<貝巴>，八府民歲當輸食鹽米鈔。

translations.literal: More than ten native chieftaincies each year owed tribute horses, corvée silver, and sea cowries, and the people of the eight prefectures each year owed grain, salt, rice, and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten native chieftaincies owed annual tribute of horses, corvée silver, and cowrie shells, while the people of the eight prefectures owed annual deliveries of grain, salt, rice, and paper notes.

sentences.zh: 至景泰初，皆積逋不能償。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Jingtai all had accumulated arrears and could not pay.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of the Jingtai reign all had fallen far behind and could not make payment.

sentences.zh: 銓等為言除之。

translations.literal: Quan and others memorialized asking that these obligations be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and his colleagues memorialized asking that these levies be remitted.

sentences.zh: 治行聞，賜誥旌異。

translations.literal: His governance and conduct became known, and he was granted an edict of commendation for outstanding service.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his governance spread, the court granted him a commendatory edict honoring his exceptional service.

sentences.zh: 景泰七年，九載滿，當入都，軍民乞留。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jingtai, when nine years in office were complete and he was due to enter the capital, soldiers and civilians begged that he be kept.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jingtai, when his nine-year term was complete and he was due to report to the capital, soldiers and civilians petitioned to keep him.

sentences.zh: 命還任。

translations.literal: He was ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 天順四年與梁楘等舉政績卓異。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun he was cited with Liang You and others for outstanding administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianshun he was commended with Liang You and others for outstanding administrative achievement.

sentences.zh: 戶部初闕尚書，王翺欲擢銓。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue first lacked a minister, Wang Ao wished to elevate Quan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue first had no minister in place, Wang Ao wanted to promote Quan to the post.

sentences.zh: 帝問李賢，賢曰：「聞其名，未見其人也。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Li Xian; Xian said, "I have heard his name but have not yet seen the man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Li Xian, who replied, "I have heard his name but have never met him.

sentences.zh: 」及是來覲，帝命賢視之，還奏貌寢。

translations.literal: "When he then came to audience, the emperor ordered Xian to observe him; returning, Xian reported that his appearance was unprepossessing.
translations.idiomatic: "When Quan then came to court for audience, the emperor had Xian look him over; on returning Xian reported that his appearance was rather homely.

sentences.zh: 乃以為右副都御史巡撫山東，尋兼撫河南。

translations.literal: He was therefore made right vice chief censor and touring pacification commissioner of Shandong, and soon also pacified Henan concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was therefore appointed right vice chief censor and touring pacification commissioner of Shandong, and soon given concurrent charge of Henan as well.

sentences.zh: 山東歲侵，請召還清軍御史。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered crop failure that year; he requested that the censor conducting military household inspections be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong suffered a bad harvest that year, he requested that the censor clearing military registers be recalled.

sentences.zh: 河南饑，請停征課馬。

translations.literal: Henan suffered famine; he requested suspension of the levy of tribute horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan suffered famine he requested that the levy of tribute horses be suspended.

sentences.zh: 皆許之。

translations.literal: All were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 成化初，左都御史李秉督師遼東，召銓署院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, when left chief censor Li Bing commanded troops in Liaodong, Quan was summoned to handle affairs of the censorate in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chenghua reign, when left chief censor Li Bing took command in Liaodong, Quan was summoned to administer the censorate in his absence.

sentences.zh: 中官唐慎等從征荊、襄還，杖死淮安知事谷淵，自奏丐免。

translations.literal: The eunuch Tang Shen and others, returning from campaigning in Jing and Xiang, beat to death Gu Yuan, an official of Huai'an, and memorialized on their own behalf asking to be exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Tang Shen and others, returning from the Jing and Xiang campaign, beat Huai'an official Gu Yuan to death and then memorialized asking to be spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 銓請罪之。

translations.literal: Quan requested that they be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Quan memorialized asking that they be punished.

sentences.zh: 乃付慎等司禮監，命法司罪其從人。

translations.literal: They were then handed over to the Directorate of Ceremonial, and the judicial offices were ordered to punish their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the others were handed over to the Directorate of Ceremonial, and the judicial authorities were ordered to punish their followers.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 謚恭靖。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Gongjing, "Respectful and Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 銓在雲南，治行為一時冠。

translations.literal: Quan in Yunnan had governance and conduct that ranked first for the age.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan Quan's record of governance was the finest of his generation.

sentences.zh: 比為巡撫，清靜不自表暴，吏民亦安之。

translations.literal: When he became a touring pacification commissioner he was quiet and restrained and did not display himself aggressively, and officials and people alike were settled by it.
translations.idiomatic: As a touring pacification commissioner he governed quietly without ostentation, and officials and commoners alike were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 王宇，字仲宏，祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, styled Zhonghong, was a man of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, styled Zhonghong, came from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 童丱時，日記萬言，巡撫侍郎于謙奇之。

translations.literal: In his childhood he could write ten thousand characters a day from memory; touring pacification vice minister Yu Qian regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he could compose ten thousand characters a day from memory; touring pacification vice minister Yu Qian was greatly impressed by him.

sentences.zh: 登正統四年進士，授南京戶部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Zhengtong and was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Zhengtong and was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當轉郎中，吏部以宇才，特用為撫州知府。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was due to be transferred to bureau director, but the Ministry of Personnel, because of Yu's talent, specially appointed him prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was due for promotion to bureau director, but the Ministry of Personnel, impressed by Yu's ability, instead appointed him prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政簡靜，而鋤強遏奸，凜不可犯，一府大治。

translations.literal: His governance was simple and quiet, yet he uprooted the powerful and checked the wicked; his stern authority could not be violated, and the whole prefecture was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was plain and restrained, yet he crushed the powerful and checked wrongdoing with an authority none dared defy, and the whole prefecture was brought to good order.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，所司上其治行，詔賜誥命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun the responsible office reported his governance and conduct, and an edict granted him a patent of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun his superiors reported his record of governance, and the court issued him a commendatory patent.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢山東右布政使，命撫恤所屬饑民。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to right administration commissioner of Shandong and ordered to comfort and relieve the famine-stricken people under his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to right administration commissioner of Shandong and ordered to relieve the famine victims in his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 明年遷右副都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to right vice chief censor and touring pacification commissioner of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made right vice chief censor and touring pacification commissioner of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 中官嚴順、都督張林等令家人承納芻糧。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yan Shun, regional commander Zhang Lin, and others had their household members take contracts to supply fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yan Shun, regional commander Zhang Lin, and others had their retainers take contracts to supply fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 宇劾奏。

translations.literal: Yu impeached and memorialized against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu impeached them by memorial.

sentences.zh: 都御史寇深為解，帝切責深。

translations.literal: Chief censor Kou Shen spoke in their defense, and the emperor sharply rebuked Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Chief censor Kou Shen tried to shield them, and the emperor sharply rebuked Shen.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼撫大同。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to pacify Datong concurrently as well.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent charge of Datong as well.

sentences.zh: 石亨及從子彪驕恣，大同其舊鎮地，征索尤橫。

translations.literal: Shi Heng and his nephew Biao were arrogant and willful; Datong was their old garrison territory, and their exactions were especially overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and his nephew Biao were arrogant and overbearing; Datong was their old power base, and their exactions there were especially ruthless.

sentences.zh: 宇抗疏論其奸，乞置之法。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a forthright memorial discussing their wickedness and begged that they be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a bold memorial denouncing their misconduct and asking that they be punished by law.

sentences.zh: 疏雖不行，聞者敬憚。

translations.literal: Although the memorial was not acted upon, those who heard of it respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Although the memorial was not acted on, all who heard of it regarded him with respect and awe.

sentences.zh: 督餉郎中楊益不能備芻槁，為宇所劾。

translations.literal: Yang Yi, a bureau director supervising supplies, could not provide sufficient fodder and was impeached by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Supply supervisor Yang Yi failed to provide adequate fodder and was impeached by Yu.

sentences.zh: 戶部庇之，宇並劾尚書沈固等。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue shielded him, and Yu also impeached Minister Shen Gu and others.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue shielded Yang, Yu also impeached Minister Shen Gu and others.

sentences.zh: 皆輸罪。

translations.literal: All admitted guilt.
translations.idiomatic: All of them pleaded guilty.

sentences.zh: 遭喪，起復為大理卿。

translations.literal: When bereavement struck he was recalled from mourning and restored as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After a bereavement he was recalled from mourning and appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 固辭，不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined, but was not permitted to do so.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined, but the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 宇剛介，所至有盛名。

translations.literal: Yu was upright and uncompromising, and wherever he went he enjoyed a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was upright and unyielding, and he earned a formidable reputation wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 居大理，平反為多。

translations.literal: While serving at the Court of Judicial Review he reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: At the Court of Judicial Review he overturned many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 崔恭，字克讓，廣宗人。

translations.literal: Cui Gong, styled Kerang, was a man of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong, styled Kerang, came from Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 正統元年進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the first year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the first year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出理延綏倉儲，有能聲。

translations.literal: Sent out to manage the granaries of Yan-Sui, he gained a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to manage the Yan-Sui granaries, he earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 以楊溥薦，擢萊州知府。

translations.literal: On Yang Pu's recommendation he was promoted to prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Yang Pu, he was promoted to prefect of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 內地輸遼東布，悉貯郡庫，歲久朽敝，守者多破家。

translations.literal: Cloth supplied from the interior for Liaodong was all stored in the prefectural treasury; after years it rotted and decayed, and those charged with guarding it often ruined their families.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth levied from the interior for Liaodong was stored in the prefectural treasury; over the years it rotted away, and the officials responsible for guarding it often ruined their families.

sentences.zh: 恭別構屋三十楹貯之，請約計歲輸外，余以充本府軍餉，遂放遣守者八百人。

translations.literal: Gong separately built thirty bays of storehouses to hold it, requested that beyond the fixed annual delivery the remainder be used for this prefecture's military rations, and then released eight hundred guards.
translations.idiomatic: Gong built thirty storehouse bays to hold the cloth, arranged that anything beyond the fixed annual delivery be used for the prefecture's military rations, and dismissed eight hundred guards.

sentences.zh: 也先犯京師，遣民兵數千入援。

translations.literal: When Esen attacked the capital he dispatched several thousand militiamen to reinforce it.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen attacked the capital he sent several thousand militiamen to reinforce the defense.

sentences.zh: 廷議城臨清，檄發役夫。

translations.literal: The court debated fortifying Linqing and issued orders mobilizing corvée laborers.
translations.idiomatic: When the court decided to fortify Linqing, it issued orders mobilizing corvée laborers.

sentences.zh: 恭以方春民乏食，請俟秋成。

translations.literal: Gong, because it was spring and the people lacked food, requested that the work wait until the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Gong argued that since it was spring and the people were short of food, the work should wait until after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 居府六年，萊人以比漢楊震。

translations.literal: After six years in the prefecture the people of Laizhou compared him to Yang Zhen of Han.
translations.idiomatic: After six years as prefect the people of Laizhou ranked him with the Han dynasty's Yang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，超遷湖廣右布政使。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign he was abruptly promoted to right administration commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he was suddenly promoted to right administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 諸司供給，率取之民。

translations.literal: The supplies of the various offices were generally taken from the people.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices routinely extracted their supplies from the people.

sentences.zh: 恭與僚佐約，悉罷之。

translations.literal: Gong made an agreement with his subordinates and abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gong agreed with his subordinates to abolish all such extractions.

sentences.zh: 公安、監利流民擅相殺。

translations.literal: Migrant people in Gong'an and Jianli killed one another at will.
translations.idiomatic: Migrant communities in Gong'an and Jianli were killing one another with impunity.

sentences.zh: 恭下令願附籍者聽，否則迨秋遣歸，眾遂定。

translations.literal: Gong issued orders that those willing to register locally were permitted to do so; otherwise they would be sent home after autumn, and the people were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gong ordered that those willing to register locally might stay, while the rest would be sent home after autumn, and the disturbance subsided.

sentences.zh: 尋遷江西左布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to left administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to left administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 司有廣濟庫，官吏幹沒五十萬。

translations.literal: The office had a Guangji treasury in which officials embezzled five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial administration maintained a Guangji treasury from which officials had embezzled five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 恭白於巡撫韓雍，典守者鹹獲罪。

translations.literal: Gong reported it to touring pacification commissioner Han Yong, and those in charge were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gong reported the matter to touring pacification commissioner Han Yong, and all those responsible were punished.

sentences.zh: 定均徭法，酌輕重，十年一役，遂為定例。

translations.literal: He fixed a balanced corvée law, weighing lighter and heavier burdens, with one service every ten years, and this became a fixed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He established a balanced corvée system, weighing lighter and heavier obligations and fixing service at once every ten years, which thereafter became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，寧王奠培不法，恭劾之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun Prince Mo of Ning, Dian Pei, acted unlawfully, and Gong impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshun Prince Mo of Ning, Dian Pei, acted unlawfully, and Gong impeached him.

sentences.zh: 削其護衛，王稍戢。
