translations.literal: His guard corps was stripped away, and the prince moderated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's guard corps was removed, and he restrained himself somewhat.

sentences.zh: 遷右副都御史，代李秉巡撫蘇、松諸府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief and replaced Li Bing as touring pacification commissioner of Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and succeeded Li Bing as touring pacification commissioner of Suzhou, Songjiang, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 按部，進耆老言利病，為興革。

translations.literal: On inspection rounds he advanced the elders to speak of benefits and harms, and undertook reforms.
translations.idiomatic: On his inspection tours he sought out village elders to hear what helped and what harmed the people, and instituted reforms accordingly.

sentences.zh: 與都督徐恭浚儀真漕河，又浚常、鎮河，避江險。

translations.literal: Together with regional commander Xu Gong he dredged the Yizhen canal transport river, and also dredged the Chang and Zhen rivers to avoid the dangers of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Together with regional commander Xu Gong he dredged the canal at Yizhen and also cleared the waterways of Changzhou and Zhenjiang to bypass the dangers of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 已，大治吳淞江。

translations.literal: Thereafter he greatly repaired the Wusong River.
translations.idiomatic: He then undertook a major project on the Wusong River.

sentences.zh: 起昆山夏界口，至上海白鶴江，又自白鶴江至嘉定卞家渡，迄莊家涇，凡浚萬四千二百余丈。

translations.literal: Starting from Xiajiekou in Kunshan to Baihe River in Shanghai, and again from Baihe River to Bianjiadu in Jiading, reaching Zhuangjia Stream, dredging altogether more than fourteen thousand two hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The work ran from Xiajiekou in Kunshan to Baihe River in Shanghai, then from Baihe River to Bianjiadu in Jiading and on to Zhuangjia Stream — more than fourteen thousand two hundred zhang dredged in all.

sentences.zh: 又浚曹家港、蒲匯塘、新涇諸水。

translations.literal: He also dredged Caojiagang, Puhuitang, Xinjing, and other waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged Caojiagang, Puhuitang, Xinjing, and other channels.

sentences.zh: 民賴其利，目曹家港為「都堂浦」。

translations.literal: The people relied on the benefit and called Caojiagang the "Commissioner's Stream."
translations.idiomatic: The people benefited greatly and nicknamed Caojiagang the "Commissioner's Stream."

sentences.zh: 初，周忱奏定耗羨則例，李秉改定以賦之輕重遞盈縮。

translations.literal: At first Zhou Chen had memorialized to fix the surtax formula for wastage and surplus; Li Bing revised it so that increase and decrease followed the lightness and heaviness of the tax assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen had originally fixed the formula for surcharges on grain wastage and surplus; Li Bing had revised it so that rates rose and fell according to the weight of each assessment.

sentences.zh: 其例甚平，而難於稽算，吏不勝煩擾。

translations.literal: The formula was very fair, but difficult to audit and calculate, and clerks could not bear the trouble and harassment.
translations.idiomatic: The revised rates were equitable in principle, but the calculations were burdensome and clerks were driven to distraction by the paperwork.

sentences.zh: 恭乃罷去，悉如忱舊。

translations.literal: Gong then abolished it and restored everything to Chen's old rules.
translations.idiomatic: Gong abolished Li Bing's system and restored Zhou Chen's original rules in full.

sentences.zh: 吏部缺右侍郎，李賢、王翺舉恭。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel lacked a right vice minister; Li Xian and Wang Ao recommended Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel fell vacant, Li Xian and Wang Ao recommended Gong.

sentences.zh: 遂召用。

translations.literal: He was thereupon summoned and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and appointed.

sentences.zh: 置「勸懲簿」，有聞皆識之。

translations.literal: He established a "Record of Encouragement and Admonition," recording everything he heard.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a "Record of Encouragement and Admonition" in which he noted every report that reached him.

sentences.zh: 翺甚倚恭，轉左。

translations.literal: Ao relied heavily on Gong and had him transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao relied heavily on Gong and had him moved to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 父憂起復。

translations.literal: On mourning for his father he returned to office before the period of mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he left office to mourn, but was recalled before the mourning period was complete.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，乞致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, he petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 成化五年，尚書李秉罷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua Minister Li Bing was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chenghua, Minister Li Bing was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 商輅欲用姚夔，彭時欲用王概，而北人居言路者，謂時實逐秉，喧謗於朝。

translations.literal: Shang Lu wished to appoint Yao Kui; Peng Shi wished to appoint Wang Gai; but northerners in the remonstrance offices said Shi had in fact driven Bing out, and raised an uproar at court.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Lu favored Yao Kui for the post; Peng Shi favored Wang Gai. Northerners among the remonstrance officials, however, claimed that Peng Shi had really forced Li Bing out, and the court was soon buzzing with accusation.

sentences.zh: 時稱疾不出，侍讀尹直以時、概皆已鄉人，恐因此得罪，急言於輅，以恭代秉。

translations.literal: Shi pleaded illness and did not attend; attendant reader Yin Zhi, because Shi and Gai were both fellow townsmen, feared they would be implicated in guilt, and urgently spoke to Lu to have Gong replace Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi pleaded illness and stayed away from court. Attendant reader Yin Zhi, fearing that Peng Shi and Wang Gai — both natives of the same region — would be caught up in the backlash, urgently advised Shang Lu to appoint Gong in Li Bing's place.

sentences.zh: 越五月，母喪歸。

translations.literal: After five months his mother died and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Five months later his mother died and he returned home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 服除，起南京吏部，劾罷諸司不識者數人。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and impeached and dismissed several incompetent officers of various offices.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete he was appointed to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, where he impeached and removed several incompetent officials.

sentences.zh: 十一年春命參贊機務。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he was ordered to participate in deliberations on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was appointed to assist in managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 居三年，致仕。

translations.literal: After three years he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚莊敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhuangmin ("Dignified and Keen").

sentences.zh: 劉孜，字顯孜，萬安人。

translations.literal: Liu Zi, styled Xianzi, was a native of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zi, styled Xianzi, was a native of Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 正統十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the tenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 授御史，出按遼東。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor and sent out to inspect Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor and dispatched to inspect Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，有建南遷議者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi ascended the throne, there were those who proposed relocating the capital south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, some at court proposed moving the capital south.

sentences.zh: 孜馳奏，乞斬言者以定人心。

translations.literal: Zi rushed in a memorial begging to execute those who spoke thus to settle the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zi sent an urgent memorial asking that the advocates be executed to steady public morale.

sentences.zh: 期滿當代，朝議邊務方殷，復留一歲。

translations.literal: When his term expired and a successor was due, the court judged border affairs still pressing and kept him for another year.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired and he was due to be replaced, the court — with border affairs still urgent — kept him on for another year.

sentences.zh: 再按畿輔。

translations.literal: He inspected the capital region a second time.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted a second inspection tour of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 時方築淪州城，以孜言罷。

translations.literal: At the time Lunzhou city was being built; because of Zi's memorial it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Work was then underway on the walls of Cangzhou; at Zi's urging the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 擢山東按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，吏部舉天下治行卓異，按察使惟孜一人，遷左布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun the Ministry of Personnel recommended outstanding administrators throughout the realm; among surveillance commissioners only Zi alone was chosen, and he was transferred to left administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianshun the Ministry of Personnel singled out officials of outstanding conduct across the empire; among surveillance commissioners Liu Zi alone was chosen, and he was promoted to left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年春，以右副都御史巡撫江南十府。

translations.literal: The next spring, as right vice censor-in-chief he toured and pacified ten prefectures of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and touring pacification commissioner of ten Jiangnan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松財賦，自周忱立法後，代者多紛更。

translations.literal: The revenues of Suzhou and Songjiang, since Zhou Chen established the law, had been frequently changed by successive replacements.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhou Chen had set the tax system for Suzhou and Songjiang, nearly every successor had tinkered with it.

sentences.zh: 孜首訪忱遺積，斟酌行之，民稱便。

translations.literal: Zi first investigated Chen's remaining legacy, weighed it, and put it into practice; the people called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zi first studied what Zhou Chen had left behind, adapted it judiciously, and the people found the result greatly to their benefit.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，應天饑，方振貸，而江北饑民就食者眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua there was famine in Yingtian; relief was just being distributed when many famine victims from north of the river came seeking food.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua famine struck Yingtian. Relief was already underway when large numbers of starving people from north of the Yangtze arrived seeking food.

sentences.zh: 孜請盡發諸縣廩，全活無算。

translations.literal: Zi requested that all county granaries be fully opened; innumerable lives were wholly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Zi petitioned to open every county granary to the full; countless lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 時民間多積困：瀕江官田久廢沒，仍責輸賦；

translations.literal: At the time many accumulated hardships afflicted the people: riverside official fields long abandoned and submerged still had tax levied upon them;
translations.idiomatic: The people were burdened by many longstanding abuses: long-submerged official fields along the river were still taxed;

sentences.zh: 蘇、松、杭、嘉諸府僉補富戶；

translations.literal: the prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, and Jiaxing conscripted wealthy households as substitutes;
translations.idiomatic: wealthy households in Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, and Jiaxing were arbitrarily pressed into tax service;

sentences.zh: 南京廊房既傾圮，猶征鈔；

translations.literal: Nanjing corridor shops already collapsed still had paper money levied;
translations.idiomatic: corridor shops in Nanjing that had already collapsed were still assessed for tax in paper notes;

sentences.zh: 上元、江寧農民代河泊所綱戶采鰣魚；

translations.literal: farmers of Shangyuan and Jiangning gathered shad in place of the net households of the river depot;
translations.idiomatic: farmers in Shangyuan and Jiangning were compelled to catch shad on behalf of the river depot's fishing households;

sentences.zh: 應天都稅宣課諸司額外增稅；

translations.literal: the Yingtian metropolitan tax office and the Xuan tax office among others added extra levies beyond quota;
translations.idiomatic: the Yingtian metropolitan tax bureau and other offices such as the Xuan tax bureau levied surcharges beyond their quotas;

sentences.zh: 江陰諸縣民戶償納荒租；

translations.literal: households in Jiangyin and other counties paid for delinquent rents on waste land;
translations.idiomatic: households in Jiangyin and other counties were forced to pay taxes on long-abandoned fields;

sentences.zh: 六合、江浦官牛歲征犢。

translations.literal: official oxen in Liuhe and Jiangpu yearly had calves levied.
translations.idiomatic: official ox herds in Liuhe and Jiangpu were taxed each year for calves.

sentences.zh: 孜皆疏罷之。

translations.literal: Zi memorialized to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zi memorialized to abolish every one of these practices.

sentences.zh: 召拜南京刑部尚書，以宋傑代。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed minister of justice at Nanjing; Song Jie replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed minister of justice at Nanjing, with Song Jie succeeding him as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年致仕，道卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he retired; he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in the fourth year and died en route.

sentences.zh: 孜廉慎，治事精審。

translations.literal: Zi was incorrupt and cautious, precise and thorough in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was scrupulously honest and careful, and handled affairs with precision.

sentences.zh: 然持法過嚴，時議其刻。

translations.literal: Yet he enforced the law excessively strictly, and contemporaries criticized him as harsh.
translations.idiomatic: But he enforced the law with excessive rigor, and contemporaries considered him unyielding.

sentences.zh: 傑為人長者。

translations.literal: Jie was by nature a man of forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jie was a man of gentle forbearance.

sentences.zh: 居二年，罷去，而邢宥代。

translations.literal: After two years he was dismissed and left office, and Xing You replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was removed from office and replaced by Xing You.

sentences.zh: 宥，文昌人。

translations.literal: You was a native of Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xing You was a native of Wenchang.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 授御史，出巡福建。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor and sent to inspect Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor and dispatched on an inspection tour of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 民十人被誣為盜，當刑呼冤。

translations.literal: Ten commoners were falsely accused as bandits; as punishment was about to be applied they cried out their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Ten men had been falsely accused of banditry; at the moment of sentencing they cried out that they were innocent.

sentences.zh: 宥為緩之，果得真盜。

translations.literal: You suspended the case for them, and indeed the real bandits were found.
translations.idiomatic: You stayed their execution, and the real culprits were soon found.

sentences.zh: 天順中，出為臺州知府，有治績。

translations.literal: In the Tianshun reign he went out as prefect of Taizhou and had governing achievements.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign he served as prefect of Taizhou with distinction.

sentences.zh: 坐累謫晉江丞。

translations.literal: Through implication in another's offense he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was implicated in another official's offense and demoted to assistant magistrate of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 憲宗復其職，改知蘇州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong restored his office and transferred him to administer Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne his rank was restored and he was appointed prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 奸民攬納秋賦，置之法，得其贓萬緡，以隄沙河，甓官道。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners monopolized collection of autumn taxes; he punished them by law, obtaining their bribes of ten thousand strings of cash, and used them to embank the Sha River and pave the official road with brick.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted corrupt agents who had monopolized collection of the autumn grain tax, confiscated bribes totaling ten thousand strings of cash, and used the funds to build embankments along the Sha River and pave the official highway with brick.

sentences.zh: 大水，民饑，不待奏輒發米二十萬斛以振。

translations.literal: Great flood; the people starved; without awaiting memorial approval he promptly issued two hundred thousand hu of grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When severe flooding brought famine, he did not wait for imperial approval before releasing two hundred thousand hu of grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 宥素廉介，及治蘇，嚴而不苛。

translations.literal: You had always been incorrupt and upright; when governing Suzhou he was strict but not harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Xing You had always been incorrupt and upright; as prefect of Suzhou he was firm without being oppressive.

sentences.zh: 傑薦於朝，詔加浙江左參政仍理府事，賜璽書。

translations.literal: Jie recommended him at court; an edict added him as left administration vice commissioner of Zhejiang while he still handled prefectural affairs, and granted him an imperial sealed letter.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jie recommended him at court; the emperor promoted him to left administration vice commissioner of Zhejiang while allowing him to retain charge of Suzhou, and bestowed on him an imperial sealed letter of appointment.

sentences.zh: 居半歲，遂以右僉都御史代傑巡撫。

translations.literal: After half a year he was then made right assistant censor-in-chief to replace Jie as touring pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Half a year later he was appointed right assistant censor-in-chief and succeeded Song Jie as touring pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開丹陽河，築奔牛閘，省兌運冗費，民以為便。

translations.literal: He opened the Danyang River, built the Benniu sluice, saved redundant costs of grain transport exchange, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Danyang River and built the Benniu sluice, cutting redundant costs from the grain transport system, to the great benefit of the people.

sentences.zh: 尋兼理兩浙鹽政，考察屬吏，奏黜不識者百七十余人。

translations.literal: Soon he also concurrently managed the salt administration of the two Zhejiangs, examined subordinate officials, and memorialized to dismiss more than one hundred seventy incompetents.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of salt administration in both Zhejiangs as well, inspected subordinate officials, and memorialized for the dismissal of more than one hundred seventy incompetents.

sentences.zh: 居數載，引疾歸。

translations.literal: After several years he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 李侃，字希正，東安人。

translations.literal: Li Kan, styled Xizheng, was a native of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kan, styled Xizheng, was a native of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the seventh year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventh year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，陳簡將才、募民壯、用戰車三事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing served as regent, he presented three matters: selecting general talent, recruiting stalwart commoners, and employing war chariots.
translations.idiomatic: While the Jing Emperor served as regent, Kan memorialized on three matters: selecting capable generals, recruiting able-bodied civilians, and deploying war chariots.

sentences.zh: 也先逼京師議者欲焚城外馬草。

translations.literal: When Esen pressed upon the capital, those in deliberation wished to burn the horse fodder outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen threatened the capital, some at court proposed burning the fodder stored outside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 侃言敵輕剽，無持久心，乞勿焚，免復斂為民累。

translations.literal: Kan said the enemy was light and swift, without enduring intent, and begged that it not be burned, lest collecting it again become a burden on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Kan argued that the enemy was raiding lightly and would not linger, and urged that the fodder be spared lest the people be taxed again to replace it.

sentences.zh: 皆報許。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 時父母在容城，侃曉夜悲泣，乞假，冒險迎之。

translations.literal: At the time his parents were in Rongcheng; Kan wept day and night in grief, begged leave, and braved danger to bring them back.
translations.idiomatic: His parents were trapped in Rongcheng; Kan wept day and night, took leave, and risked his life to bring them to safety.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，議錄扈從死事諸臣後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, deliberation arose on ennobling the descendants of ministers who died in attendance on the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign the court debated ennobling the descendants of officials who had died in the emperor's service during the crisis.

sentences.zh: 侃因言避難偷生者，宜嚴譴以厲臣節。

translations.literal: Kan thereupon said those who fled difficulty and saved themselves by stealth should be sternly censured to sharpen ministerial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Kan added that officials who had fled and saved themselves should be sternly punished to uphold the standard of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 上皇將還，與同官劉福等言禮宜從厚。

translations.literal: When the retired emperor was about to return, he spoke with colleagues Liu Fu and others that the rites should be generous.
translations.idiomatic: When the former emperor was about to return from captivity, Kan and his colleagues Liu Fu and others argued that he should be received with full ceremonial honors.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，被詰，尚書胡濙為解，乃已。

translations.literal: He ran counter to the imperial will, was rebuked, Minister Hu Ying explained on his behalf, and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the emperor, and Kan was called to account; Minister Hu Ying interceded for him and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 再遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 軍興，減天下學校師儒俸廩。

translations.literal: With military campaigns arising, the salaries and grain rations of teachers throughout the realm were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out, stipends for teachers at schools throughout the empire were cut.

sentences.zh: 侃奏復之。

translations.literal: Kan memorialized to restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Kan memorialized for their restoration.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書金濂違詔征租，侃論濂，下之吏。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Jin Lian violated the edict in collecting rents; Kan impeached Lian and had him handed to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Revenue Jin Lian collected rents in violation of an imperial edict, Kan impeached him and had the case referred to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 石亨從子彪侵民業，侃請置重典，並嚴禁勛戚、中官不得豪奪細民，有司隱者同罪。

translations.literal: Shi Heng's nephew Biao encroached on the people's property; Kan requested severe punishment, and also strictly forbade meritorious relatives and eunuchs from seizing commoners' holdings by force, with officials who concealed such acts sharing the same guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Heng's nephew Biao seized commoners' land, Kan called for heavy penalties and urged a strict ban on meritorious nobles and eunuchs wresting property from ordinary people, with equal punishment for officials who looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 帝宥亨、彪，余如其請。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned Heng and Biao; the rest followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Shi Heng and Biao, but granted the remainder of Kan's requests.

sentences.zh: 時給事中敢言者，林聰稱首，侃亦矯抗有直聲。

translations.literal: At the time among supervising secretaries who dared speak out, Lin Cong was foremost; Kan also was upright and unyielding and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Among the outspoken supervising secretaries of the day, Lin Cong was foremost; Kan too was boldly upright and earned a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 廷議易儲，諸大臣唯唯。

translations.literal: At court they deliberated on changing the heir; the great ministers assented murmuringly.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated replacing the crown prince, the senior ministers nodded assent in silence.

sentences.zh: 侃泣言東宮無失德，聰與御史朱英亦言不可，時議壯之。

translations.literal: Kan wept and said the Eastern Palace had no fault in virtue; Cong and censor Zhu Ying also said it was impossible; contemporaries praised their courage.
translations.idiomatic: Kan wept and declared that the crown prince had done nothing wrong; Lin Cong and censor Zhu Ying spoke against the change as well, and contemporaries applauded their courage.

sentences.zh: 擢詹事府丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 天順元年改太常丞，進太仆卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he was changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 明年復設山西巡撫，遷侃右僉都御史任之。

translations.literal: The next year the Shanxi touring pacification commission was reestablished; Kan was transferred to right assistant censor-in-chief to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the post of touring pacification commissioner of Shanxi was restored, and Kan was appointed right assistant censor-in-chief to fill it.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「塞北之地，與窮荒無異。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: "The lands north of the passes differ little from utter wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "The lands beyond the northern frontier are scarcely distinguishable from utter wilderness.

sentences.zh: 非生長其間者，未有能寧居而狎敵者也。

translations.literal: None but those raised there can dwell in peace and grow familiar with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Only those raised in such country can dwell there in peace and grow accustomed to facing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今南人戍西北邊，怯風寒，聞寇股栗。

translations.literal: Now southerners garrison the northwest frontier, fearing wind and cold; at word of raiders their legs tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners now garrison the northwest frontier: they cannot endure the wind and cold, and at word of an enemy raid they tremble with fear.

sentences.zh: 而北人戍南，亦不耐暑，多潛逃。

translations.literal: Northerners garrisoning the south likewise cannot bear the heat, and many flee in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners posted to garrison the south cannot bear the heat either, and many desert their posts.

sentences.zh: 宜令南北清勾之軍，各就本土補伍，人情交便，戎備得修。

translations.literal: It is proper to order soldiers cleared and mustered from north and south each to fill ranks in their native regions; human sentiment would mutually benefit, and frontier defense would be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers from both north and south who have been cleared from the rolls should be assigned to fill vacancies in their home regions. This would suit men better on both sides, and frontier defenses would be properly maintained.

sentences.zh: 」時不能用。

translations.literal: " At the time it could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not act on the proposal at that time.

sentences.zh: 奏發巡按李傑罪，傑亦訐侃。

translations.literal: He memorialized to expose the crimes of touring inspector Li Jie; Jie also denounced Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized exposing the crimes of the touring inspector Li Jie, and Jie in turn accused Kan.

sentences.zh: 按傑事有驗，除名。

translations.literal: Investigation of Jie's case found substance; he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation confirmed the charges against Jie, and he was dismissed and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 侃無贓罪，獲宥。

translations.literal: Kan had no bribery guilt and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: No corruption was found against Kan, and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 六年考察屬吏，奏罷布政使王允、李正芳以下百六十人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he inspected subordinate officials and memorialized to dismiss one hundred sixty persons from administration commissioner Wang Yun and Li Zhengfang downward.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of his tenure he reviewed subordinate officials and memorialized for the dismissal of one hundred sixty men, from the administration commissioners Wang Yun and Li Zhengfang on down.

sentences.zh: 因言：「諸臣年與臣若、不堪任事者，臣悉退之，臣亦當罷。

translations.literal: He added: "Among the officials whose age is like mine and who are unfit for office, I would dismiss them all; I too ought to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Any official of my age who is no longer fit for office should be removed—and I should be removed as well.

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: " An edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 侃性剛方，力振風紀，貪墨者屏跡。

translations.literal: Kan's nature was stern and upright; he vigorously restored discipline, and the corrupt withdrew from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was stern and upright by nature. He vigorously restored public discipline, and the corrupt dared not show themselves.

sentences.zh: 其年冬以母喪歸，軍民擁泣，至不得行。

translations.literal: That winter, returning home on his mother's death, soldiers and civilians crowded around weeping until he could not depart.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when he left to observe mourning for his mother, soldiers and civilians thronged around him weeping until he could hardly make his way through.

sentences.zh: 服除，遂不出，家居十余年卒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he did not go out again; he remained at home for more than ten years and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he never returned to office, and after more than ten years at home he died.

sentences.zh: 侃事親孝，好學安貧，歿幾不能殮。

translations.literal: Kan was filial toward his parents, loved learning, and was content in poverty; at death he could barely afford burial.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was filial toward his parents, devoted to learning, and content with poverty; at his death his family could scarcely afford his funeral.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，國子生江紀等言，前祭酒胡儼，都御史高明、李侃學行事功，彰著耳目，並乞賜謚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, National University students Jiang Ji and others said that former libationer Hu Yan, censor-in-chief Gao Ming, and Li Kan in learning, conduct, and achievement were conspicuous to all eyes, and together begged posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign, National University students led by Jiang Ji petitioned that the former libationer Hu Yan, the censor-in-chief Gao Ming, and Li Kan had distinguished themselves in learning, conduct, and public service, and asked that posthumous titles be granted to all three.

sentences.zh: 寢不行。

translations.literal: The matter was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The petition was shelved and nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 侃二子：德恢，嚴州知府；

translations.literal: Kan's two sons: Dehui, prefect of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Kan had two sons: Dehui, prefect of Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 德仁，河東鹽運使。

translations.literal: Deren, salt transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: and Deren, salt transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 雷復，字景昜，湖廣寧遠人。

translations.literal: Lei Fu, styled Jingyang, was a native of Ningyuan in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Fu, styled Jingyang, was a native of Ningyuan in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 正統初進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi at the beginning of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination early in the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人，歷官廣西副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier and served through the post of Guangxi vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier and rose to become vice commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 藤縣民胡趙成構瑤陷縣治，復與參將範信討斬之。

translations.literal: The Teng County commoner Hu Zhaocheng incited the Yao to seize the county seat; Fu, together with regional commander Fan Xin, attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When a Teng County man named Hu Zhaocheng incited Yao tribesmen to overrun the county seat, Fu joined regional commander Fan Xin in a punitive campaign and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 成化初以大臣會薦，擢山東右布政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, through joint recommendation by senior ministers, he was promoted to right administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he was promoted to right administration commissioner of Shandong on the joint recommendation of senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 七年征拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed right vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned to the capital and appointed right vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋改右副都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 繼李侃後，端恪守法，得軍民心。

translations.literal: Following Li Kan, he was upright and conscientious in observing the law and won the hearts of soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Succeeding Li Kan in the post, he governed with upright integrity, strictly observed the law, and won the trust of both soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 敗寇紅沙煙，再敗之煙寺溝、石人村，賜敕獎勞。

translations.literal: He defeated bandits at Hongsha Pass and again defeated them at Yansi Gully and Shiren Village, and was granted an imperial letter of commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated bandits at Hongsha Pass and again routed them at Yansi Gully and Shiren Village, for which he received an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 時山西大浸，而廷議以陜西用兵，令預征芻餉，轉輸榆林。

translations.literal: At the time Shanxi suffered severe flooding, yet court deliberation, because of military operations in Shaanxi, ordered advance collection of fodder and provisions for transport to Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi was then suffering severe floods, yet the court, because of the war in Shaanxi, ordered fodder and provisions collected in advance and transported to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 復上言：「自山西至榆林，道路險絕，民賫銀往易，價騰湧，不免稱貸，償責多破產。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized further: "From Shanxi to Yulin the roads are perilous and cut off; the people carry silver to exchange for goods, prices surge, they cannot avoid borrowing on credit, and many are ruined repaying debts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized: "The route from Shanxi to Yulin is treacherous and remote. People must carry silver to buy supplies, prices have soared, and many who borrow to meet the demand are ruined when the debts come due.

sentences.zh: 今雨雪愆違，饑民疾病流離，困悴萬狀，而應輸綾帛、藥果諸物，又不下萬計。

translations.literal: Now rain and snow are untimely; starving people are sick and displaced in every wretched condition, yet the silk, medicine, fruit, and other items due for delivery number no less than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Rain and snow have come at the wrong season; the hungry are sick and displaced in every imaginable misery, yet the tribute of silk, medicine, fruit, and other goods still due runs to tens of thousands of items.

sentences.zh: 乞依山東例蠲除，仍發帑振贍。

translations.literal: I beg that, following the Shandong precedent, these levies be remitted and treasury funds still be issued for relief and support.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these levies be remitted as was done in Shandong, and that treasury funds be released for relief.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 及發金三萬不足，請鬻鹽四十萬引，並令民入粟授散官。

translations.literal: When the disbursement of thirty thousand taels of silver proved insufficient, he requested the sale of four hundred thousand salt certificates and also that the people be allowed to contribute grain in exchange for honorary offices.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand taels from the treasury proved insufficient, he asked permission to sell four hundred thousand salt certificates and to accept grain contributions from the people in return for honorary rank.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All his requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 十年夏卒於官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, summer, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the tenth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 原傑，字子英，陽城人。

translations.literal: Yuan Jie, styled Ziying, was a native of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jie, styled Ziying, was a native of Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 正統十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the tenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 又二年，授南京御史，尋改北。

translations.literal: Two years later he was appointed censor at Nanjing, and soon transferred to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed a censor at Nanjing, and was soon transferred to the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 巡按江西，捕誅劇盜，奸宄斂跡。

translations.literal: Touring and inspecting Jiangxi, he captured and executed major bandits, and evildoers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: As touring inspector of Jiangxi he captured and executed major bandits, and lawlessness subsided.

sentences.zh: 復按順天諸府。

translations.literal: He again inspected the prefectures of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He next served as touring inspector of the Shuntian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大水，牧官馬者乏芻，馬多斃，有司責償，傑請免之。

translations.literal: In great flood, those tending official horses lacked fodder and many horses died; the responsible offices demanded compensation, and Jie requested exemption.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe flood, keepers of government horses ran out of fodder and many horses died; when the local offices demanded compensation, Jie petitioned for the charges to be waived.

sentences.zh: 開中鹽引入米振饑。

translations.literal: He opened salt certificates in exchange for grain to relieve famine.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the salt-certificate system to accept grain contributions in exchange for relief during the famine.

sentences.zh: 疏入，為部所格，景帝卒從傑議。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was blocked by the ministry, but the Jingdi emperor finally followed Jie's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry blocked his memorial at first, but the Jingdi emperor eventually adopted Jie's proposal.

sentences.zh: 超擢江西按察使。

translations.literal: He was exceptionally promoted to Jiangxi surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted out of turn to surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 發寧王奠培淫亂事，革其護衛。

translations.literal: He exposed the lewd misconduct of Prince Ning, Dianpei, and abolished his guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed the Prince of Ning, Dianpei, for licentious conduct and had his personal guard abolished.

sentences.zh: 治行聞，賜誥旌異，遷山東左布政使。

translations.literal: His governance and conduct became known; he was granted an imperial patent commending his exceptional service and was transferred to left administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his governance spread, he was granted an imperial patent commending his exceptional service and was made left administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 成化二年就拜右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he was immediately appointed right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Chenghua reign he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shandong on the spot.

sentences.zh: 歲兇振救，民無流移。

translations.literal: In years of famine he provided relief, and the people did not flee.
translations.idiomatic: In years of crop failure he organized relief so effectively that the people did not flee the region.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as left vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as left vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時黃河遷決不常，彼陷則此淤。

translations.literal: At the time the Yellow River shifted and breached without fixed pattern; where one section collapsed, another silted up.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River then shifted and broke its banks unpredictably; where one stretch collapsed, another silted up.

sentences.zh: 軍民就淤墾種。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians reclaimed and planted on the silted land.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians began farming the newly silted land.

sentences.zh: 奸徒指為園場屯地，獻王府邀賞，王府輒據有之。

translations.literal: Wicked men pointed to it as garden grounds and garrison lands, presented it to princely establishments to seek reward, and the establishments promptly seized possession.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers declared the land princely garden or garrison property, offered it to imperial clansmen in hope of reward, and the princes promptly seized it.

sentences.zh: 傑請獻者謫戍，並罪受獻者。

translations.literal: Jie requested that those who presented land be banished to frontier service and that those who accepted presentations also be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jie proposed that those who offered such land be banished to military service on the frontier and that those who accepted it be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 江西盜起，以傑嘗再蒞其地得民，詔往治。

translations.literal: Bandits arose in Jiangxi; because Jie had twice governed that region and won the people, an edict ordered him to go and handle it.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out in Jiangxi, the emperor sent Jie to deal with it, knowing that he had governed the province twice before and enjoyed the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 捕戮六百余人，余悉解散。

translations.literal: He captured and killed more than six hundred men, and the rest were all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed more than six hundred men and dispersed the rest.

sentences.zh: 改左副都御史，還佐院事。

translations.literal: He was changed to left vice censor-in-chief and returned to assist in censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice censor-in-chief and returned to assist in the affairs of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄流民數十萬，朝廷以為憂。

translations.literal: Migrant populations in Jingzhou and Xiangyang numbered several hundred thousand, and the court regarded this with concern.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred thousand displaced people had gathered in the Jing and Xiang regions, and the court was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 祭酒周洪謨嘗著《流民圖說》，謂當增置府縣，聽附籍為編氓，可實襄、鄧戶口，俾數百年無患。

translations.literal: Libationer Zhou Hongmo once wrote 《A Treatise on Migrant Populations with Maps》, saying that prefectures and counties should be added and migrants allowed to register as attached commoners, thereby filling the household rolls of Xiangyang and Dengzhou and keeping the region free of trouble for several centuries.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer Zhou Hongmo had written 《A Treatise on Migrant Populations with Maps》, arguing that new prefectures and counties should be created and migrants allowed to register locally as ordinary subjects, thereby strengthening the population of Xiangyang and Dengzhou and securing the region for centuries to come.

sentences.zh: 都御史李賓以聞，帝善之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Li Bin reported it, and the emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Bin forwarded the proposal, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遂命傑出撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Jie was then ordered out to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Jie was dispatched to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 遍歷山溪，宣朝廷德意，諸流民欣然願附籍。

translations.literal: He traveled throughout mountains and streams, proclaiming the court's benevolent intent, and all the migrants gladly wished to register.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling through the mountains and river valleys, he proclaimed the court's benevolent intentions, and the migrants gladly offered to register.

sentences.zh: 於是大會湖廣、河南、陜西撫、按官籍之，得戶十一萬三千有奇，口四十三萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he convened the grand coordinators and touring inspectors of Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi to register them, obtaining more than one hundred thirteen thousand households and more than four hundred thirty-eight thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He then convened the grand coordinators and touring inspectors of Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi to register the population, recording more than 113,000 households and 438,000 persons.

sentences.zh: 其初至，無產及平時頑梗者，驅還其鄉，而附籍者用輕則定田賦。

translations.literal: Those who had just arrived without property, and those ordinarily stubborn and refractory, were driven back to their native places, while those who registered were assessed land tax under lighter rules.
translations.idiomatic: Recent arrivals without property and habitual troublemakers were sent back to their home districts, while those who registered were given lighter land-tax assessments.

sentences.zh: 民大悅。

translations.literal: The people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 因相地勢，以襄陽所轄鄖縣，居竹、房、上津、商、洛諸縣中，道路四達，去襄陽五百余裏。

translations.literal: Accordingly, considering the terrain, Yun County under Xiangyang lay among the counties of Zhu, Fang, Shangjin, Shang, and Luo; roads ran in all directions, yet it was more than five hundred li from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the terrain, he noted that Yun County, under Xiangyang's jurisdiction, lay among the counties of Zhushan, Fang, Shangjin, Shang, and Luo. Though roads ran in all directions, it was more than five hundred li from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 山林阻深，將吏鮮至，猝有盜賊，府難遙制。

translations.literal: Mountains and forests were deep and obstructive; officers and officials rarely arrived, and if bandits suddenly appeared, the prefecture could not control them from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains and forests were rugged and remote, officials seldom reached the area, and if bandits struck suddenly the prefecture could not control matters from so far away.

sentences.zh: 乃拓其城，置鄖陽府，以縣附之。

translations.literal: He therefore expanded its walls, established Yunyang Prefecture, and attached the county to it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore expanded the county seat, established Yunyang Prefecture, and made the county its seat.

sentences.zh: 且置湖廣行都司，增兵設戍，而析竹山置竹溪，析鄖置鄖西，析漢中之洵陽置白河，與竹山、上津、房鹹隸新府。

translations.literal: Moreover he established the Huguang regional military commission, increased troops and set garrisons, split off Zhuxi from Zhushan, Yuxi from Yun, and Baihe from Xunyang in Hanzhong, and together with Zhushan, Shangjin, and Fang County made them subordinate to the new prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also established a regional military commission for Huguang, increased garrisons, carved Zhuxi out of Zhushan, Yuxi out of Yun, and Baihe out of Xunyang in Hanzhong, and placed these together with Zhushan, Shangjin, and Fang County under the new prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又於西安增山陽，南陽增南召、桐柏，汝州增伊陽，各隸其舊府。

translations.literal: Further, in Xi'an he added Shanyang; in Nanyang he added Nanzhao and Tongbai; in Ruzhou he added Yiyang; each remained subordinate to its former prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also created Shanyang under Xi'an, Nanzhao and Tongbai under Nanyang, and Yiyang under Ruzhou, each remaining under its original prefecture.

sentences.zh: 制既定，薦知鄧州吳遠為鄖陽知府，諸縣皆擇鄰境良吏為之。

translations.literal: Once the system was settled, he recommended Wu Yuan, magistrate of Dengzhou, as prefect of Yunyang, and for all the counties chose capable officials from neighboring jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new arrangements were in place, he recommended Wu Yuan, magistrate of Dengzhou, as prefect of Yunyang and selected capable officials from neighboring districts to serve as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 流人得所，四境乂安。

translations.literal: The displaced found places to settle, and the four borders were governed in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The migrants found settled homes, and peace was restored throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 將還，以地界湖廣、河南、陜西，事無統紀，因薦御史吳道宏自代。

translations.literal: About to return, because the territory bordered Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi and affairs lacked unified oversight, he recommended censor Wu Daohong to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to return, he saw that the region straddled Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi and needed unified oversight, and so recommended Censor Wu Daohong to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 詔即擢道宏大理少卿，撫治鄖陽、襄陽、荊州、南陽、西安、漢中六府。

translations.literal: An edict immediately promoted Daohong to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and charged him with pacification and governance of the six prefectures of Yunyang, Xiangyang, Jingzhou, Nanyang, Xi'an, and Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately promoted Wu Daohong to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and charged him with overseeing pacification in the six prefectures of Yunyang, Xiangyang, Jingzhou, Nanyang, Xi'an, and Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 鄖陽之有撫治，自此始也。

translations.literal: The pacification superintendency of Yunyang began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the office of pacification superintendent for Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 傑以功進右都御史。

translations.literal: Jie was advanced to right censor-in-chief for his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement Jie was promoted to right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 傑數揚歷於外，既居內臺，不欲出。

translations.literal: Jie had served many times in the field; once he held office on the inner censorate, he did not wish to go out again.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had served repeatedly in the provinces, and once he held a post at the capital Censorate he did not wish to leave again.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄之命，非其意也。

translations.literal: The Jing and Xiang appointment was not to his wish.
translations.idiomatic: The assignment to the Jing and Xiang region was not what he had wanted.

sentences.zh: 事竣，急請還朝。

translations.literal: When the task was finished, he urgently requested return to court.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the work was done he urgently petitioned to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會南京兵部缺尚書，以傑任之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ministry of War at Nanjing lacked a minister, and Jie was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of minister of war at Nanjing fell vacant, Jie was appointed to fill it.

sentences.zh: 傑疏辭。

translations.literal: Jie memorialized to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Jie memorialized declining the appointment.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 遂卒於南陽，年六十一。

translations.literal: He then died at Nanyang, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Nanyang at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 鄖、襄民為立祠，詔贈太子太保，錄其子宗敏為國子生。

translations.literal: The people of Yun and Xiang erected shrines for him; an edict posthumously granted him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and enrolled his son Zongmin as a National University student.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yunyang and Xiangyang erected shrines in his honor. The emperor posthumously granted him the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and enrolled his son Zongmin in the National University.

sentences.zh: 彭誼，字景宜，東莞人。

translations.literal: Peng Yi, styled Jingyi, was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yi, styled Jingyi, was a native of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 正統中，由鄉舉除工部司務。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong, through provincial recommendation he was appointed registrar of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he entered service through the provincial examination and was appointed registrar of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘗與尚書辯事，無所阿。

translations.literal: He once debated affairs with the minister and did not defer at all.
translations.idiomatic: He once debated policy with his minister and would not yield or flatter.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，用薦改御史。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi emperor ascended, through recommendation he was changed to censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi emperor came to the throne he was made a censor on recommendation.

sentences.zh: 從尚書石璞塞沙灣決河，進秩二等。

translations.literal: Following Minister Shi Pu in blocking the breach at Shawan on the Yellow River, he was advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted Minister of Works Shi Pu in repairing the Shawan breach on the Yellow River and was promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 復決，再往塞之。

translations.literal: When it breached again, he went again to block it.
translations.idiomatic: When the river broke through again he returned to repair the breach once more.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年，以從大學士王文巡視江、淮，擒獲蘇州賊，擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai, for following Grand Secretary Wang Wen in inspecting the Yangzi and Huai regions and capturing Suzhou bandits, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Jingtai reign he accompanied Grand Secretary Wang Wen on an inspection of the Yangzi and Huai regions, helped capture bandits in Suzhou, and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時年二月擢右僉都御史，提督紫荊、倒馬諸關。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and put in charge of Zijing Pass, Daoma Pass, and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of that year he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and placed in charge of Zijing Pass, Daoma Pass, and other frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 劾都指揮胡璽納賄縱軍罪。

translations.literal: He impeached regional commander Hu Xi for the crimes of accepting bribes and letting troops run wild.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached regional commander Hu Xi for accepting bribes and allowing his troops to run wild.

sentences.zh: 天順初，罷巡撫官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, the grand coordinator post was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign the post of grand coordinator was abolished.

sentences.zh: 中朝有不悅誼者，下遷紹興知府。

translations.literal: Some at court who disliked Yi had him demoted to prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies at court had him demoted to prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，輒發廩振貸。

translations.literal: In years of famine he promptly opened granaries for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he promptly opened the granaries to provide relief grain on loan.

sentences.zh: 吏白當俟朝命，誼曰：「民方急，安得循故事耶？

translations.literal: An official reported that he ought to await court command; Yi said: "The people are in urgent need—how can one follow precedent?
translations.idiomatic: When an aide said he should wait for orders from the capital, Yi replied: "The people are in desperate need—how can I wait for precedent?

sentences.zh: 」築白馬閘障海潮。

translations.literal: " He built the White Horse Sluice to block sea tides.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the White Horse Sluice to hold back the tide.

sentences.zh: 歷九載，多惠政。

translations.literal: Over nine years he had many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: During nine years in office he carried out many policies that benefited the people.

sentences.zh: 超擢山東左布政使，入為工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was exceptionally promoted to left administration commissioner of Shandong and entered service as left vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted out of turn to left administration commissioner of Shandong and then summoned to the capital as left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，遼東巡撫張岐得罪，吏部舉代者。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua, the grand coordinator of Liaodong, Zhang Qi, offended and was punished; the Ministry of Personnel proposed replacements.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Chenghua reign the grand coordinator of Liaodong, Zhang Qi, fell from favor, and the Ministry of Personnel proposed candidates to replace him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遼東自王翺後，屢更巡撫，多不稱，可於大臣中求之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Since Wang Ao in Liaodong, grand coordinators have been changed repeatedly and many have been unsuitable; one may be sought among senior ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Since Wang Ao served in Liaodong, we have changed grand coordinators repeatedly, and most have proved unsuitable. We should look among the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 」乃改誼右副都御史以往，鎮守中官橫征諸屬衛。

translations.literal: " Yi was then changed to right vice censor-in-chief and sent there; the eunuch in charge of defense levied exactions on all subordinate guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was accordingly made right vice censor-in-chief and sent to Liaodong, where the eunuch charged with frontier defense was extorting the subordinate guards.

sentences.zh: 誼下令，凡文牒不經巡撫審定者，所司毋輒行，虐焰為息。

translations.literal: Yi issued an order that any document not reviewed and approved by the grand coordinator must not be acted on by the relevant offices, and the tyrannical abuse then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ordered that no document might be executed unless the grand coordinator had reviewed and approved it, and the reign of extortion came to an end.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，戶部檄所司開黑山金場。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, winter, the Ministry of Revenue ordered the relevant offices to open the Heishan gold field.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year the Ministry of Revenue ordered the local offices to reopen the Heishan gold mines.

sentences.zh: 誼奏永樂中太監王彥等開是山，督夫六千人，三閱月止得金八兩，請罷之。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized that during the Yongle reign the eunuch Wang Yan and others had opened that mountain, conscripted six thousand laborers, and in three months obtained only eight liang of gold, and requested that the project be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported that in the Yongle era the eunuch Wang Yan and others had worked that same mountain with six thousand conscripted laborers and, after three months, had recovered only eight liang of gold. He asked that the operation be shut down.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 誼好古博學，通律歷、占象、水利、兵法之屬。

translations.literal: Yi loved antiquity and was broadly learned, versed in calendrics, astrology, hydraulic engineering, military strategy, and related fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a lover of antiquity and a wide-ranging scholar, fluent in calendrics, astrology, hydraulic works, military strategy, and kindred subjects.

sentences.zh: 平居謙厚簡默，臨事毅然有斷。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was modest, sincere, and sparing of speech; when affairs arose he was resolute and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was humble, warm, and quiet; when business came before him he acted with firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 鎮遼八年，軍令振肅。

translations.literal: During eight years governing Liaodong, military discipline was restored and stern.
translations.idiomatic: In eight years on the Liaodong frontier he restored military discipline to its full rigor.

sentences.zh: 年未老，四疏告歸，家居四十余年卒。

translations.literal: Though not yet old, he submitted four memorials requesting retirement; he lived at home for more than forty years before dying.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had grown old he submitted four memorials asking to retire, lived at home for more than forty years, and then died.

sentences.zh: 牟俸，巴人。

translations.literal: Mou Feng was a native of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Feng was from Ba.

sentences.zh: 景泰初進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi at the beginning of the Jingtai reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination early in the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史，巡按雲南。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor and toured and inspected Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a censor and sent to inspect Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 南寧伯毛勝鎮金齒，俸列其違縱罪，將吏皆聳。

translations.literal: The Earl of Nanning, Mao Sheng, was stationed at Jinchi; Feng listed his crimes of violation and indulgence, and all the generals and officials were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Nanning, Mao Sheng, held Jinchi. Feng laid out his crimes of disobedience and lax command, and every officer in the command stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 天順元年出為福建僉事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he was sent out as assistant commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianshun reign he was posted to Fujian as an assistant commissioner.

sentences.zh: 成化初，進秩副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was promoted in rank to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷江西按察使，政尚嚴厲，入為太仆卿。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to be surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi; his administration valued severity, and he entered the capital as Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was moved to Jiangxi as surveillance commissioner, where his rule was stern. He was then summoned to the capital as Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 八年以左僉都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, as left vice censor-in-chief, he served as grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed grand coordinator of Shandong with the rank of left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 歲祲，請發濟南倉儲減價以糶，令臨清關稅收米麥濟振。

translations.literal: The year suffered crop failure; he requested that grain stores in Jinan be opened and sold at reduced prices, and that customs duties at Linqing be collected in rice and wheat for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the harvest failed that year, he asked that Jinan's granaries be opened and grain sold at reduced prices, and that customs at Linqing accept rice and wheat in payment of duties for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved every request.

sentences.zh: 時大饑，雖獲振，饑民眾，轉徙益多。

translations.literal: There was great famine at the time; although relief was obtained, the starving population was large and migration increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: Famine was severe. Relief helped, but the starving were still countless, and more and more people drifted from place to place.

sentences.zh: 俸請敕鄰境撫、按隨所在安輯，秋成資遣復業。

translations.literal: Feng requested an edict that grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners in neighboring regions settle and pacify the refugees wherever they were found, and after the autumn harvest assist them to return home and resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Feng asked for an imperial order directing neighboring grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners to settle refugees wherever they were found and, once the autumn harvest came in, help them return home and resume their work.

sentences.zh: 又乞開中淮、浙鹽百萬引，盡蠲州縣逋課。

translations.literal: He also petitioned to open commercial salt sales in Huai and Zhejiang totaling one million ding, and to remit entirely the overdue taxes of prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to open one million salt certificates under the grain-for-salt system in Huai and Zhejiang, and to cancel all overdue tax payments owed by prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 詔如所請，更命移臨清倉粟十萬石振之。

translations.literal: An edict granted his requests and further ordered one hundred thousand shi of grain moved from the Linqing granary for relief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his requests and further ordered one hundred thousand shi of grain transferred from the Linqing granary for relief.

sentences.zh: 至七月，俸又言公私困竭，救荒靡策，乞開納粟例，令胥吏得就選，富民授散官，且截留漕糧備振。

translations.literal: By the seventh month Feng again reported that public and private resources were exhausted and there was no strategy for famine relief; he petitioned to open the precedent of contributing grain for office, allowing clerks to qualify for appointment, granting wealthy men honorary offices, and retaining grain tribute transport for relief reserves.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month Feng reported again that public and private resources were exhausted and that famine relief had no further remedy. He asked to revive the grain-donation precedent so clerks could qualify for office, wealthy men could receive honorary ranks, and grain from the tribute transport could be held back for relief.

sentences.zh: 十月復言：「今救荒者止救其饑，不謀其寒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he again memorialized: "Present famine relief only addresses hunger, not cold.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he wrote again: "Relief today feeds the hungry but does nothing for the cold.

sentences.zh: 縱得食，終不免僵死，乞貸貧民布棉。

translations.literal: Even if people obtain food, they will still die frozen; I beg that cloth and cotton be loaned to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Even with food in hand, people will still freeze to death. I ask that cloth and cotton be loaned to the poor.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆嘉納。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 俸又檄發東昌、濟寧倉粟十萬余石為軍士月糧，而以德州、臨清寄庫銀易米振濟，奏請伏專擅罪。

translations.literal: Feng also ordered the release of more than one hundred thousand shi of grain from the Dongchang and Jining granaries as monthly rations for soldiers, and used silver held in depots at Dezhou and Linqing to purchase rice for relief; he submitted a memorial asking to accept punishment for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Feng also ordered more than one hundred thousand shi of grain released from the Dongchang and Jining granaries as monthly rations for the troops, and used silver held in the Dezhou and Linqing treasuries to buy rice for relief. He then submitted a memorial asking to be punished for having acted without authorization.

sentences.zh: 帝特宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor expressly pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 已，復以俸奏免柴夫折價銀，移河南輸邊粟濟山東，而別給銀為邊餉，山東輸京租二十萬石，給本地用。

translations.literal: Soon after, Feng again memorialized to exempt the silver commutation payment for fuel-bearer corvée, to transfer Henan's border-supply grain to relieve Shandong while providing silver separately for frontier rations, and to leave two hundred thousand shi of Shandong's tribute grain destined for the capital for local use.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Feng memorialized again to abolish the silver commutation for firewood-bearer corvée, to divert Henan's frontier grain shipments to relieve Shandong while paying the frontier garrisons in silver instead, and to retain two hundred thousand shi of Shandong's tribute grain destined for the capital for local use.

sentences.zh: 十年又饑，請發倉儲出貸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year famine struck again; he requested that stores be opened for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: When famine returned in the tenth year, he asked that the granaries be opened and grain lent out for relief.

sentences.zh: 撫山東五年，盡心荒政，活饑民不可勝數。

translations.literal: Over five years as coordinator of Shandong he devoted himself to famine administration and saved countless starving people.
translations.idiomatic: In five years as grand coordinator of Shandong he gave himself wholly to famine relief and saved more starving people than could be counted.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史改撫蘇、松。

translations.literal: As right vice censor-in-chief he was transferred to govern Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 俸性嚴。

translations.literal: Feng's nature was stern.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was stern by nature.

sentences.zh: 以所部多巨室，欲故摧抑之，乃禁索私租，勸富家出谷備振動千計，怨謗紛然。

translations.literal: Because his jurisdiction had many great clans, he wished deliberately to suppress them; he forbade the collecting of private rents, urged wealthy families to contribute grain for relief by the thousands, and complaints and slander arose on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Because his jurisdiction held many great families, he deliberately sought to bring them down. He banned the collection of private rents and pressed wealthy households to contribute thousands of measures of grain for relief, and resentment and slander spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 中官汪直有事南京，或譖俸。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Zhi had business in Nanjing; someone slandered Feng to him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Zhi was on business in Nanjing, and someone denounced Feng to him.

sentences.zh: 直歸，未發也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi returned but had not yet acted on it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi returned to court but had not yet moved against him.

sentences.zh: 俸初在山東，與布政陳鉞負氣不相下。

translations.literal: Earlier in Shandong, Feng and administration commissioner Chen Yue, both proud of temper, would not yield to each other.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng had been in Shandong, he and the administration commissioner Chen Yue, both proud men, had refused to defer to each other.

sentences.zh: 後鉞從容言俸短，直信之。

translations.literal: Later Chen Yue spoke calmly of Feng's faults, and Wang Zhi believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chen Yue spoke at leisure of Feng's failings, and Wang Zhi believed every word.

sentences.zh: 十四年，俸議事至京，直請執俸下詔獄。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when Feng came to the capital on official business, Wang Zhi requested that Feng be seized and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Feng came to the capital on official business, and Wang Zhi asked that he be seized and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 先是，所親學士江朝宗除服還朝，俸迓之九江，聯舟並下。

translations.literal: Previously, his close associate Academician Jiang Chaozong, having finished mourning, was returning to court; Feng met him at Jiujiang and they traveled downriver in linked boats.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, his close friend the academician Jiang Chaozong, having finished mourning, was returning to court. Feng met him at Jiujiang, and they traveled downriver in linked boats.

sentences.zh: 所至，有司供張頗盛。

translations.literal: Wherever they went, local officials provided lavish hospitality.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they stopped, local officials entertained them with lavish hospitality.

sentences.zh: 直因謂朝宗有所關說，並下獄。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi therefore claimed Jiang Chaozong had been lobbying on someone's behalf, and both were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi then claimed that Jiang Chaozong had been pulling strings for someone, and had both men thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 詞連僉事吳扁等十余人，俱被逮。

translations.literal: The case implicated assistant commissioner Wu Bian and more than ten others; all were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The case dragged in the assistant commissioner Wu Bian and more than ten others, all of whom were arrested.

sentences.zh: 系獄半歲，謫戍湖廣。

translations.literal: After half a year in prison they were banished to serve in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year in prison they were banished to military service in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 俸在江西時，共成許聰獄，人多議其深文。

translations.literal: When Feng was in Jiangxi, he jointly prosecuted the Xu Cong case; many criticized him for stretching the law.
translations.idiomatic: While Feng was in Jiangxi he had helped build the case against Xu Cong, and many criticized him for twisting the law.

sentences.zh: 至是被禍，皆知為直誣，然無白其冤者。

translations.literal: When he suffered this disaster, all knew he had been framed by Wang Zhi, yet no one cleared his name.
translations.idiomatic: When this disaster fell on him, everyone knew Wang Zhi had framed him, yet no one spoke up to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒戍所。

translations.literal: A year later he died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 夏壎，字宗成，天臺人。

translations.literal: Xia Xun, styled Zongcheng, was a native of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Xun, styled Zongcheng, was from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 天順初，巡按福建，繼清軍江西，發鎮守中官葉達恣橫狀，達為斂威。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he toured Fujian; he then inspected troops in Jiangxi and exposed the rampant conduct of the eunuch Ye Da, who was stationed in defense; Ye Da consequently restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he inspected Fujian, then reviewed troops in Jiangxi and exposed the abuses of the frontier eunuch Ye Da, who thereafter checked his conduct.

sentences.zh: 以薦超擢廣東按察使。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was promoted out of turn to surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was promoted out of turn to surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時用師歲久，役民守城，壎至悉遣之。

translations.literal: Troops had been deployed for years; civilians were conscripted to guard the walls; when Xun arrived he sent them all home.
translations.idiomatic: The army had been in the field for years, and civilians had been conscripted to man the walls. When Xun arrived he sent them all home.

sentences.zh: 成化初，奏：「瑤、僮弗靖，用兵無功，由有司撫字乖方，賊因得誘良民為徒黨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he memorialized: "The Yao and Zhuang peoples are unsettled; military campaigns have achieved nothing because local officials govern wrongly, and bandits have been able to lure good people into their gangs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he memorialized: "The Yao and Zhuang are unsettled, and military campaigns have failed because local officials have governed badly. Bandits have therefore been able to lure good people into their ranks.

sentences.zh: 劇寇數百，脅從萬千，進則驅之當前，退則殺以抒憤，害常在民，而利常在彼。

translations.literal: The chief bandits number only in the hundreds, but those coerced to follow them are in the thousands; when advancing they drive these people ahead as shields, when retreating they kill them to vent their rage—the harm always falls on the people, while the profit always falls on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The hard core of bandits numbers only in the hundreds, yet those coerced to follow them run into the thousands. When they advance they drive these people ahead as shields; when they retreat they kill them to vent their rage. The harm always falls on the people, while the profit always falls on the bandits.

sentences.zh: 況用兵不已，供斂日增。

translations.literal: Moreover, as warfare continues without end, levies and exactions increase daily.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as the fighting goes on without end, levies and exactions grow heavier every day.

sentences.zh: 以易搖之人心，責無窮之軍費。

translations.literal: With easily swayed hearts among the people, one cannot meet endless military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: With hearts so easily shaken among the people, one cannot meet endless military expenses.

sentences.zh: 恐外患未除，內變先作。

translations.literal: I fear that before external troubles are removed, internal turmoil will break out first.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that before the external threat is removed, internal disorder will break out first.

sentences.zh: 請慎選監司守令，撫綏遺民，彼被脅之眾自聞風來歸。

translations.literal: I request that supervisory officials and prefectural and county magistrates be carefully chosen, that displaced people be pacified and comforted, and that those coerced into following the bandits will then come back of their own accord when they hear of this policy.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that circuit supervisors and prefectural and county magistrates be chosen with care, that displaced people be settled and comforted, and that those coerced into following the bandits will then come back of their own accord when they hear of it.

sentences.zh: 」帝深納其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 尋遷布政使，調江西。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to administration commissioner and assigned to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to administration commissioner and transferred to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 八年以右副都御史巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, as right vice censor-in-chief, he served as grand coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed grand coordinator of Sichuan with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 苗、僚時為寇。

translations.literal: Miao and Lao people at times raided as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Miao and Lao raiders struck from time to time.

sentences.zh: 壎立互知會捕法，賊為之戢。

translations.literal: Xun established the mutual-notification system for joint pursuit and capture; the bandits therefore restrained themselves.
