translations.idiomatic: Xun instituted a system of mutual notification for joint pursuit and capture, and the bandits accordingly checked themselves.

sentences.zh: 古州苗萬余，居爛土久，時議逐之，壎謂非計。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Miao of Guzhou had long lived on barren land; there was talk of expelling them; Xun said this was not a sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Miao of Guzhou had long lived on poor wasteland, and some proposed driving them out. Xun said that would be no solution.

sentences.zh: 松潘參將堯彧請益戍兵三千，又力陳不可。

translations.literal: The deputy commander of Songpan, Yao Yu, requested three thousand additional garrison troops; Xun again forcefully argued this was inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: When the deputy commander of Songpan, Yao Yu, asked for three thousand additional garrison troops, Xun again argued forcefully against it.

sentences.zh: 皆得寢。

translations.literal: Both proposals were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were dropped.

sentences.zh: 已，奏所部將校多犯法，奏請逾時，輒至遁逸。

translations.literal: Soon after, he reported that many officers under his jurisdiction broke the law and, because memorials took too long, they often escaped before arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he reported that many officers under his command broke the law and, because memorials took too long to reach the throne, often fled before they could be arrested.

sentences.zh: 請先逮系，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: He requested that they be arrested and detained first, then reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that offenders be arrested and detained first, and only then reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝可之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 壎剛介，善聽斷，所至民不冤。

translations.literal: Xun was upright and uncompromising, skilled in hearing cases and reaching judgment; wherever he went the people were not wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was upright and unyielding, skilled at hearing cases and reaching judgment; wherever he served, the people were not wronged.

sentences.zh: 在蜀二年，民夷畏服。

translations.literal: During two years in Shu, both Chinese and non-Chinese peoples feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: In two years in Shu, both Chinese and non-Chinese peoples feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 然厭繁劇，與時多齟齬。

translations.literal: Yet he disliked heavy and complicated duties and often clashed with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he wearied of heavy and complicated duties and often found himself at odds with the age.

sentences.zh: 子堠獻詩勸歸，壎欣然納焉。

translations.literal: His son Hou presented a poem urging retirement; Xun gladly accepted the advice.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hou wrote a poem urging him to retire, and Xun gladly took the counsel.

sentences.zh: 年未五十，即求退。

translations.literal: Before the age of fifty he sought to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was fifty he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 章四上，得請。

translations.literal: He submitted four memorials and obtained permission.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted four memorials before his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 既歸，杜門養親，不按賓客。

translations.literal: After returning home he shut his doors to nurture his parents and did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: Once home, he shut his doors to care for his parents and refused to receive guests.

sentences.zh: 又五年卒。

translations.literal: Five years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he died.

sentences.zh: 鍭，舉進士。

translations.literal: Hou passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Hou also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年謁選入都，上書請復李文祥、鄒智等官，罷大學士劉吉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, when he went to the capital for appointment, he submitted a memorial requesting restoration of office for Li Wenxiang, Zou Zhi, and others, and the dismissal of Grand Secretary Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Hongzhi reign, when he went to the capital to await appointment, he submitted a memorial asking that Li Wenxiang, Zou Zhi, and others be restored to office and that Grand Secretary Liu Ji be removed.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，下獄，得釋。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will, was imprisoned, and was then released.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the throne, was thrown into prison, and was later released.

sentences.zh: 久之，除南京大理評事。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed reviewing officer of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was appointed reviewing officer of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 疏論賦斂、徭役、馬政、鹽課利弊及宗藩、戚裏侵漁狀。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the pros and cons of taxation, corvée labor, horse administration, and salt levies, and on encroachments by imperial clansmen and maternal relatives.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the strengths and failings of taxation, corvée labor, horse administration, and salt levies, and on the encroachments of imperial clansmen and maternal relatives.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 鍭素無宦情。

translations.literal: Hou had never had an appetite for official life.
translations.idiomatic: Hou had never cared for official life.

sentences.zh: 居官僅歲餘，念母老，乞侍養，遂歸。

translations.literal: After little more than a year in office, thinking of his aged mother, he requested leave to serve her and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year in office, mindful that his mother was old, he asked leave to care for her and went home.

sentences.zh: 家居三十余年，竟不復出。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than thirty years and never returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than thirty years and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 高明，字上達，貴溪人。

translations.literal: Gao Ming, styled Shangda, was a native of Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ming, styled Shangda, was from Guixi.

sentences.zh: 幼事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: From childhood his filial service to his mother was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 登景泰二年進士，授御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jingtai and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jingtai reign and was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 聞內苑造龍舟，切諫。

translations.literal: Learning that the inner park was building dragon boats, he remonstrated sharply.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the inner park was building dragon boats, he remonstrated sharply.

sentences.zh: 有指揮為大臣所陷，論死，辯出之。

translations.literal: A commander had been framed by a senior minister and sentenced to death; Ming argued on his behalf and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: A commander had been framed by a senior minister and sentenced to death; Ming argued on his behalf and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 徐州民訴有司於朝，時例，越訴者戍邊。

translations.literal: Commoners of Xuzhou appealed to the court against local officials; at the time the rule was that those who jumped ranks in appeal were sent to frontier exile.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners of Xuzhou appealed to the court against local officials. At the time the rule was that anyone who bypassed the usual channels of appeal was sent to frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 明言：「戍邊，防誣訴也。

translations.literal: Ming said: "Frontier exile is meant to prevent false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Ming said: "Frontier exile is meant to deter false accusations.

sentences.zh: 今訴不誣，法止當杖。

translations.literal: When the appeal is not false, the law requires only beating with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: When the appeal is not false, the law requires no more than beating with the rod.

sentences.zh: 」民有為妖言者，吏貪功，誣以謀反。

translations.literal: " Some commoners had spread sorcery tales; officials greedy for credit accused them of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Some commoners had spread sorcery tales, and officials hungry for credit accused them of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 明按無反狀，止坐妖言律。

translations.literal: Ming investigated and found no evidence of rebellion; he applied only the statute on sorcery speech.
translations.idiomatic: Ming investigated and found no evidence of rebellion; he applied only the statute on sorcery speech.

sentences.zh: 皆報許。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved every recommendation.

sentences.zh: 巡撫河南，黜屬吏六十人。

translations.literal: As grand coordinator of Henan he dismissed sixty subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinator of Henan he dismissed sixty subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 再按畿輔，入總諸道章奏。

translations.literal: On a second tour of the capital region he entered the capital to oversee memorials from all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On a second inspection tour of the capital region he entered the capital to oversee memorials from every circuit.

sentences.zh: 天順初，尚書陳汝言有罪，偕諸御史劾，下之獄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, Minister Chen Ruyan was guilty; Gao Ming together with the various censors impeached him, and Chen was put in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign Minister Chen Ruyan was found guilty; Gao Ming joined the other censors in impeaching him, and Chen was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 四年，御史趙明等劾天下朝覲官，觸帝怒，詰草疏主名。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Censor Zhao Ming and others impeached officials from throughout the realm who had come for court audience, provoking the emperor's anger; he demanded the name of whoever had drafted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhao Ming and other censors memorialized against officials from across the empire who had come to court for audience, which enraged the emperor, who demanded to know who had authored the draft.

sentences.zh: 眾大懼，明獨自承。

translations.literal: All were greatly afraid; Ming alone took responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The others were terrified; Zhao Ming alone stepped forward and admitted authorship.

sentences.zh: 都御史寇深言：「頻年章疏，盡出明手，幸勿以細故加罪。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Kou Shen said: "For years the memorials have all come from Ming's hand; I beg that you not punish him for a minor matter.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Kou Shen said: "For years every memorial has been written by Ming; please do not punish him over a trifling matter.

sentences.zh: 」帝意解，反稱明能。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was eased, and he instead praised Ming's ability.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and instead praised Ming for his competence.

sentences.zh: 石亨既誅，僮仆皆收。

translations.literal: After Shi Heng had been executed, his servants were all seized.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Heng was put to death, all his household servants were taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 明言不宜，坐免者百人。

translations.literal: Ming said this was inappropriate; on that account a hundred persons were exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Ming argued that this was wrong, and as a result a hundred people were released from liability.

sentences.zh: 擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，拜南京右僉都御史。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended the throne, he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianzong emperor came to the throne, Ming was appointed right vice censor-in-chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 以留都春夏淫雨，請修人事以回天意。

translations.literal: Because the southern capital had heavy rains in spring and summer, he asked that human affairs be set right to turn away Heaven's displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the prolonged spring and summer rains at the southern capital, he urged moral and administrative reform to answer Heaven's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 時納馬入監者至萬余人，明請區別。

translations.literal: At the time those who paid horses to enter the Imperial College numbered more than ten thousand; Ming asked that they be distinguished and sorted.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand men had bought their way into the Imperial College with horses; Ming requested that their cases be reviewed separately.

sentences.zh: 薦郎中孫瓊、陳鴻漸、梅倫、何宜，主事宋瑛，皆端方廉潔，恬於進取，宜顯擢以風有位。

translations.literal: He recommended Directors Sun Qiong, Chen Hongjian, Mei Lun, and He Yi, and Section Chief Song Ying—all upright, incorrupt, and indifferent to advancement—and said they should be conspicuously promoted to admonish those in office.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended several bureau directors and a section chief as upright, incorrupt officials who shunned self-advancement, urging that they be promoted conspicuously to set an example for officeholders.

sentences.zh: 疏下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate departments.

sentences.zh: 成化三年，揚州鹽寇起，守兵失利，詔明討之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua, salt bandits rose in Yangzhou; the garrison troops were defeated; the emperor ordered Ming to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 3 salt smugglers turned bandit in Yangzhou; after the garrison suffered defeat, Ming was ordered to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 造巨艦，名曰「籌亭」，往來江上督戰，並江置邏堡候望。

translations.literal: He built great ships called "Chou Pavilion," going back and forth on the river to supervise fighting, and established beacon forts along the river for lookout.
translations.idiomatic: He had large warships built, named Chou Pavilion, patrolled the river to direct operations, and set up lookout forts along both banks.

sentences.zh: 賊縱跡無所匿，遂平之。

translations.literal: Wherever the bandits fled they had nowhere to hide; he thus pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits could find no refuge wherever they fled, and the disturbance was pacified.

sentences.zh: 內官鬻私鹽，據法沒入，鹽政大治。

translations.literal: Inner eunuchs who sold private salt were seized by law and their goods confiscated; salt administration was greatly set in order.
translations.idiomatic: He confiscated illicit salt sold by palace eunuchs and brought salt administration under firm control.

sentences.zh: 因條上利病十余事，多議行。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted in detail more than ten items of benefit and harm; most were discussed and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized more than ten specific reforms, most of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 仍還原任，以親老乞終養歸。

translations.literal: He still returned to his original post; because his parents were old he asked leave for perpetual nursing care and went home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his former post, then sought leave to care for his aged parents and went home for good.

sentences.zh: 十四年，上杭盜發。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, bandits rose in Shanghang.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen banditry broke out in Shanghang.

sentences.zh: 詔起巡撫福建，督兵往討。

translations.literal: He was ordered to leave retirement as grand coordinator of Fujian and lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from retirement as grand coordinator of Fujian and sent with troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 擒誅首惡，余皆減死遣戍。

translations.literal: The ringleaders were captured and executed; the rest had their death sentences reduced and were sent to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: The chief culprits were captured and executed; the others received commuted sentences and were banished to garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 以上杭地接江西、廣東，盜易嘯聚，請析置永定縣。

translations.literal: Because Shanghang's territory adjoined Jiangxi and Guangdong and bandits easily gathered there, he asked that Yongding County be split off and established.
translations.idiomatic: Shanghang bordered Jiangxi and Guangdong and was prone to bandit mustering; he requested the creation of Yongding County.

sentences.zh: 移疾徑歸。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and returned home at once.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he died.

sentences.zh: 楊繼宗，字承芳，陽城人。

translations.literal: Yang Jizong, styled Chengfang, was a native of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jizong, styled Chengfang, came from Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 天順初進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi at the beginning of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination early in the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a section chief in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a section chief in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 囚多疫死，為時其食飲，令三日一櫛沐，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Many prisoners died of plague; he arranged their food and drink in good time, ordered bathing and grooming every three days, and saved very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Many inmates died of epidemic illness; he saw that they were fed on schedule, had them bathe and comb their hair every three days, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 又善辨疑獄。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at resolving doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was also adept at unraveling doubtful criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 河間獲盜，遣裏民張文、郭禮送京師，盜逸。

translations.literal: When thieves were caught in Hejian, village men Zhang Wen and Guo Li were sent to escort them to the capital; the thieves escaped.
translations.idiomatic: After bandits were captured in Hejian, two local men were dispatched to escort them to the capital, but the prisoners escaped en route.

sentences.zh: 文謂禮曰：「吾二人並當死。

translations.literal: Wen said to Li: "The two of us should both die.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen said to Guo Li: "We will both be executed.

sentences.zh: 汝母老，鮮兄弟，以我代盜，庶全汝母子命。

translations.literal: Your mother is old and you have few brothers; if I substitute for the thieves, perhaps your mother and you may keep your lives.
translations.idiomatic: Your mother is old and you have almost no brothers; let me stand in for the fugitives so that you and your mother may live.

sentences.zh: 」禮泣謝，從之。

translations.literal: " Li wept and thanked him, and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Li wept his thanks and agreed.

sentences.zh: 文桎梏詣部，繼宗察非盜，竟辨出之。

translations.literal: Wen came to the ministry in shackles; Jizong saw he was not a thief and ultimately cleared him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen presented himself in shackles at the ministry; Jizong saw he was no bandit and finally got him exonerated.

sentences.zh: 成化初，用王翺薦，擢嘉興知府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, on Wang Ao's recommendation, he was promoted to prefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he was promoted to prefect of Jiaxing on Wang Ao's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 以一仆自隨，署齋蕭然。

translations.literal: He took only one servant with him; his official quarters were austere.
translations.idiomatic: He kept only one servant; his yamen was starkly plain.

sentences.zh: 性剛廉孤峭，人莫敢犯。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern, incorrupt, solitary, and abrupt; no one dared to trifle with him.
translations.idiomatic: Stern, incorrupt, and forbiddingly upright, he brooked no familiarity from anyone.

sentences.zh: 而時時集父老問疾苦，為祛除之。

translations.literal: Yet from time to time he gathered elders to ask their hardships and removed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he regularly summoned village elders to hear their grievances and set them right.

sentences.zh: 大興社學，民間子弟八歲不就學者，罰其父兄；

translations.literal: He greatly promoted community schools; commoners' sons who at eight years did not go to school had their fathers and elder brothers punished;
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded community schools; if a boy of eight did not attend school, his father and elder brothers were fined;

sentences.zh: 遇學官以賓禮。

translations.literal: he treated school officials with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: he received school officers with the courtesy due to guests.

sentences.zh: 師儒競勸，文教大興。

translations.literal: Master-scholars competed in exhortation; cultural teaching flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers vied in their efforts, and local education flourished.

sentences.zh: 御史孔儒清軍，裏老多撻死。

translations.literal: Censor Kong Ru inspected troops; many village elders were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Kong Ru conducted a troop inspection, many village elders were flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 繼宗榜曰：「御史杖人至死者，詣府報名。

translations.literal: Jizong posted a notice: "Any censor who beats a person to death must come to the prefecture and register his name.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong posted a notice: "Any censor who flogs someone to death must report to the prefecture and give his name.

sentences.zh: 」儒怒。

translations.literal: " Ru was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ru was incensed.

sentences.zh: 繼宗入見曰：「為治有體。

translations.literal: Jizong entered to see him and said: "There is a proper form to governance.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong called on him and said: "Government has its proper structure.

sentences.zh: 公但剔奸弊，勸懲官吏。

translations.literal: Your Lordship need only root out malfeasance and encourage and chastise officials.
translations.idiomatic: Your duty is to expose wrongdoing and admonish or punish officials.

sentences.zh: 若比戶稽核，則有司事，非憲體也。

translations.literal: If you examine every household, that is the business of the regular offices, not the proper role of an investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: House-by-house scrutiny is the work of the regular administration, not the proper scope of an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 」儒不能難，而心甚銜之。

translations.literal: " Ru could not refute him, but harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ru had no reply, but he deeply resented Jizong.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，突入府署，發篋視之，敝衣數襲而已。

translations.literal: On the verge of leaving, he burst into the prefectural offices, opened chests and looked—only a few suits of worn clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he barged into the yamen, opened Jizong's chests, and found only a few threadbare garments.

sentences.zh: 儒慚而去。

translations.literal: Ru left in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ru withdrew in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 中官過者，繼宗遺以菱芡、歷書。

translations.literal: When palace eunuchs passed through, Jizong sent them water caltrop and calendar books as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs passed through, Jizong gave them water caltrops and almanacs.

sentences.zh: 中官索錢，繼宗即發牒取庫金，曰：「金具在，與我印券。

translations.literal: A eunuch demanded money; Jizong immediately issued a requisition to take gold from the treasury, saying: "The gold is all here—give me your stamped receipt.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch demanded cash, Jizong at once issued a voucher to draw gold from the treasury, saying: "The gold is ready—give me your stamped receipt.

sentences.zh: 」中官咋舌不敢受。

translations.literal: " The eunuch clucked his tongue and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch fell silent and dared not take it.

sentences.zh: 入覲，汪直欲見之，不可。

translations.literal: When he came to court for audience, Wang Zhi wished to see him; he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: During an audience visit Wang Zhi wanted to meet him; Jizong refused.

sentences.zh: 憲宗問直：「朝覲官孰廉？

translations.literal: Xianzong asked Zhi: "Which of the audience officials is incorrupt?
translations.idiomatic: The Xianzong emperor asked Wang Zhi: "Which of the officials at audience is incorrupt?

sentences.zh: 」直對曰：「天下不愛錢者，惟楊繼宗一人耳。

translations.literal: " Zhi answered: "Among all under Heaven who do not love money, there is only Yang Jizong alone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi replied: "Under Heaven, the only man who will not take money is Yang Jizong alone.

sentences.zh: 」九載秩滿，超遷浙江按察使。

translations.literal: " After nine years his term was full; he was promoted out of turn to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in office he was promoted out of turn to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 數與中官張慶忤。

translations.literal: He repeatedly clashed with the eunuch Zhang Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly crossed the eunuch Zhang Qing.

sentences.zh: 慶兄敏在司禮，每於帝前毀繼宗。

translations.literal: Qing's elder brother Min was in the Directorate of Ceremonial and often slandered Jizong before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qing's brother Min, who served in the Directorate of Ceremonial, often maligned Jizong before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「得非不私一錢之楊繼宗乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Could this not be Yang Jizong, who would not keep a single coin for himself?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Surely you do not mean Yang Jizong, who would not keep a single coin for himself?

sentences.zh: 」敏惶恐，遺書慶曰：「善遇之，上已知其人矣。

translations.literal: " Min was fearful and sent a letter to Qing saying: "Treat him well—the emperor already knows the man.
translations.idiomatic: Min was alarmed and wrote to Zhang Qing: "Treat him well—the emperor already knows what sort of man he is.

sentences.zh: 」聞母喪，立出。

translations.literal: " On hearing of his mother's death, he left office immediately.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned his mother had died, he resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 止驛亭下，盡籍廨中器物付有司。

translations.literal: He stopped at the post station; he inventoried everything in the yamen and handed it to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at the post station, listed every item in the yamen, and handed all over to the appropriate authorities.

sentences.zh: 惟攜一仆、書數卷而還。

translations.literal: He took only one servant and a few scrolls of books and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He went home with only one servant and a few books.

sentences.zh: 服除，以右僉都御史巡撫順天。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, as right vice censor-in-chief he served as grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed grand coordinator of Shuntian with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 畿內多權貴莊田，有侵民業者，輒奪還之。

translations.literal: Within the capital region there were many estates of powerful families; where they encroached on people's livelihoods, he would seize them back and return them.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered lands that powerful families in the capital region had seized from commoners.

sentences.zh: 按行關塞，武備大飭。

translations.literal: He inspected passes and fortifications; military readiness was greatly tightened.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the frontier passes and greatly strengthened defenses.

sentences.zh: 星變，應詔陳言，歷指中官及文武諸臣貪殘狀，且請召還中官出鎮者。

translations.literal: At a celestial anomaly he responded to an edict with a memorial, itemizing the greedy and cruel conduct of eunuchs and civil and military officials, and also asked that eunuchs sent out to command garrisons be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When a celestial portent appeared he memorialized at the emperor's call, denouncing corrupt eunuchs and officials and urging recall of eunuchs stationed on the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 益為權貴所嫉。

translations.literal: He was all the more envied by the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He earned still greater hatred from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 治中陳翼訐其過，權貴因中之，左遷雲南副使。

translations.literal: Administration Vice Director Chen Yi denounced his faults; the powerful framed him through this and he was demoted to vice commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: A subordinate denounced him; the elite seized the chance to ruin him, and he was demoted to vice commissioner in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，遷湖廣按察使。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended, he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaozong he was made surveillance commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 既至，命汲水百斛，洗滌廳事而後視事，曰：「吾以除穢也。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he ordered a hundred hu of water drawn to wash the main hall before taking up business, saying: "I do this to remove filth.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up his post he had a hundred hu of water brought to wash the reception hall, saying: "I am washing away the filth left behind.

sentences.zh: 」居無何，復以僉都御史巡撫雲南。

translations.literal: " Before long he was again grand coordinator of Yunnan with the rank of vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again appointed grand coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三司多舊僚，相見歡然。

translations.literal: The three provincial offices had many old colleagues; when they met they were joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials in the three provincial offices were former colleagues; they greeted one another warmly.

sentences.zh: 既而出位揖之曰：「明日有公事，諸君幸相諒。

translations.literal: Then he stepped from his seat and bowed to them, saying: "Tomorrow there will be official business; I hope you will all understand.
translations.idiomatic: Then he left his seat and bowed to them, saying: "Tomorrow we have official business; I trust you will understand.

sentences.zh: 」遂劾罷不職者八人。

translations.literal: " He then impeached and dismissed eight incompetent men.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he impeached and removed eight unfit officials.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 繼宗力持風節，而居心慈厚，自處必以禮。

translations.literal: Jizong forcefully upheld integrity; yet his heart was kindly and generous, and in his own conduct he always kept to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong held fast to integrity yet was kind at heart and always conducted himself with propriety.

sentences.zh: 為知府，謁上官必衣繡服，朝覲謁吏部亦然。

translations.literal: As prefect, when paying calls on superiors he always wore embroidered robes; when going to audience he visited the Ministry of Personnel likewise.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he wore the prescribed embroidered court dress when calling on superiors and when attending audience at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 或言不可，笑曰：「此朝廷法服也，此而不服，將安用之？

translations.literal: Some said this was improper; he laughed and said: "This is the court's statutory dress—if one does not wear it on these occasions, what is it for?
translations.idiomatic: When others objected, he laughed and said: "This is the court's prescribed dress—if I do not wear it here, what is it for?

sentences.zh: 」為浙江按察時，倉官十余人坐缺糧系獄，至鬻子女以償。

translations.literal: " When he was surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang, more than ten granary officials were imprisoned for grain shortfalls, to the point of selling children to make repayment.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang surveillance commissioner he found more than ten granary officials jailed for grain shortages, some selling their children to cover the deficit.

sentences.zh: 繼宗欲寬之而無由。

translations.literal: Jizong wished to leniently treat them but had no means.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong wanted to show mercy but saw no way to do so.

sentences.zh: 一日，送月俸至，命量之，則溢原數。

translations.literal: One day when monthly salary was delivered, he ordered it measured and found it exceeded the original amount.
translations.idiomatic: One month when his salary arrived he had it measured and found it exceeded the proper sum.

sentences.zh: 較他司亦然。

translations.literal: Comparing with other departments, it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same was true in other offices.

sentences.zh: 因悟倉吏缺糧之由，將具實以聞。

translations.literal: He thus understood the reason for the granary officials' grain shortfalls and was about to report the facts in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He realized why the granary officials were short and prepared to report the truth.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，請於繼宗，願捐俸代償。

translations.literal: All were afraid; they asked Jizong, willing to donate salary to make repayment.
translations.idiomatic: The officials panicked and begged Jizong to let them make up the difference from their own pay.

sentences.zh: 由是十人者獲釋。

translations.literal: Through this the ten men were released.
translations.idiomatic: Ten of them were thus released.

sentences.zh: 嘗監鄉試得二卷，具朝服再拜曰：「二子當大魁天下，吾為朝廷得人賀耳。

translations.literal: Once when supervising the provincial examination he obtained two answer sheets; clad in court dress he bowed twice and said: "These two youths will top the empire; I congratulate the court on gaining such men.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the provincial examinations he read two papers, put on court dress, and bowed twice, saying: "These two men will lead the empire in the examinations; I congratulate the court on finding such talent.

sentences.zh: 」及拆卷，王華、李旻也，後果相繼為狀元。

translations.literal: " When the rolls were opened, they were Wang Hua and Li Min, who indeed successively became top graduates.
translations.idiomatic: When the names were revealed they were Wang Hua and Li Min, who later became chief graduates in succession.

sentences.zh: 人服其鑒。

translations.literal: People admired his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: All marveled at his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，謚貞肅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was given the posthumous title Zhen Su (Upright and Stern).
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously titled Zhen Su.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明初以十五布政司分治天下，諸邊要害則遣侯伯勛臣鎮扼之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the beginning of the Ming, fifteen provincial administration commissions divided rule of the empire; at strategic points on the borders marquis, earls, and meritorious ministers were dispatched to hold them in check.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Early in the Ming, fifteen provincial administrations divided the empire, while marquises, earls, and meritorious nobles were posted to key frontiers.

sentences.zh: 永樂之季，敕蹇義等二十六人巡行天下，安撫軍民，事竣還朝，不為經制。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongle, twenty-six men including Jian Yi were ordered to tour the empire, pacifying troops and people; when their tasks were done they returned to court—it was not a permanent institution.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongle, twenty-six officials including Jian Yi were sent on empire-wide inspection tours; when finished they returned—this was not yet a fixed system.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，始命熊概巡撫蘇、松、兩浙。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, Xiong Gai was first ordered to serve as grand coordinator of Suzhou, Songjiang, and the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xuande Xiong Gai became the first grand coordinator of Suzhou, Songjiang, and the two Zhejiang circuits.

sentences.zh: 越數年，而江西、河南諸省以次專設巡撫官。

translations.literal: After several years, Jiangxi, Henan, and other provinces in turn had grand coordinator posts established separately.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Jiangxi, Henan, and other provinces gained dedicated grand coordinators in succession.

sentences.zh: 天順初，暫罷復設，諸邊亦稍用廷臣出鎮或參贊軍務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun they were briefly abolished and then restored; on the various frontiers court ministers were also gradually used to command garrisons or assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshun the posts were briefly abolished then restored; court ministers were gradually sent to frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 蓋以地大物眾，法令滋章，三司謹奉教條，修其常職；

translations.literal: For the realm was vast and its goods abundant, and statutes grew ever more detailed; the three provincial offices carefully followed instructions and performed their regular duties;
translations.idiomatic: The empire was vast and its population great, and regulations multiplied; the three provincial offices dutifully followed orders and handled routine affairs;

sentences.zh: 而興利除弊，均賦稅，擊貪濁，安善良，惟巡撫得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: but to promote benefit and remove harm, equalize taxes, strike at greed and corruption, and settle the good and honest—only the grand coordinator could act expediently as needed.
translations.idiomatic: yet only grand coordinators had discretionary power to promote good, remove abuses, balance taxes, punish corruption, and protect the law-abiding.

sentences.zh: 熊概以下諸人，強幹者立聲威，愷悌者流惠愛，政績均有可紀。

translations.literal: From Xiong Gai downward, the strong and capable established authority; the mild and kindly spread kindness; all had achievements worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiong Gai onward, the forceful built reputation while the gentle spread kindness—all left records worthy of note.

sentences.zh: 于謙、周忱巡撫最為有名，而勛業尤盛，故別著焉。

translations.literal: Yu Qian and Zhou Chen were most famed as grand coordinators, but their meritorious achievements were especially great, and so they are treated in separate accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian and Zhou Chen were the most celebrated coordinators, but their achievements were so great they receive separate biographies.
